## S2-29s — exact finite binary80 product with one-round packing (bounded helper)

Added `round_pack_exact_magnitude(sign, exponent, magnitude, mode)` for exact
signed `u128` magnitudes. It normalizes without loss and rounds once into a
normal or subnormal binary80 result. After normalization the high 64 bits form
the quotient and the low 64 bits form a remainder jammed as
`r=(lo>>1)|(lo&1)` over `2^63`. This preserves zero/nonzero and below/at/above-
half information; the sticky low bit prevents an odd product from being
mistaken for an exact tie. A nonzero underflow result rounded to zero preserves sign;
checked-exponent and finite-range overflow remain bounded `None` results.
`multiply_finite_to_binary80` composes the existing full-`u128`
`multiply_finite_significands` product with the new packer; it never narrows
through the signed coefficient rounder. Zero operands, exact zero, and input
bytes/provenance follow the bounded helper contract; no FMUL instruction or
guest exception semantics were added.

Focused tests cover even-magnitude equivalence, odd tails below/at/above normal
ties under all modes/signs, normal carry and minimum-normal/subnormal promotion,
minimum and half-minimum subnormal, signed underflow zero, checked-exponent and
finite-range rejection, zero/odd products, and input immutability. Verification
passed: targeted tests (3/3 and 1/1), all `od-isa` tests (1,689), workspace
all-target check, formatting, Graphify, and diff check. Independent Sol/high
review found no issues. No x87 instruction execution or physical x86 acceptance

remains open for broader x87 behavior.

## S2-29u — p64-aware large-gap binary80 addition bridge

Extended the composed `x87::add_finite_to_binary80` path for normalized,
nonzero operands whose exponent gaps exceed 64. Gaps through 64 retain the exact
`u128` alignment and one-round magnitude packer from S2-29t. Larger gaps use a
p=64-specific bridge that returns a normalized 64-bit quotient and classifies
the nonzero tail as below, exactly at, or above half. Compact representatives
1/4, 1/2, and 3/4 feed the existing rounder. Same-sign addition is below half;
for opposite signs, a dominant significand above `2^63` is above half after
subtracting a retained unit. At exactly `2^63`, gap 65 is a tie only if the
smaller significand is exactly `2^63`; a larger smaller significand moves below
half. Gaps 66 and above move above half.

The classifier is specific to p=64. Binary32/binary64 retain their prior results
and diagnostics through the `BinaryFinite` adapter. Tests cover both signs and
operand orders across every rounding mode, dominant significands above `2^63`,
gaps 65/66/127/128/32828, the old gap-65 coefficient-helper refusal,
max-finite with signed minimum subnormals, gap-64 compatibility, zero,
cancellation, and input immutability.

## S2-29v — pure finite x87 square root helper

Added `x87::sqrt_finite_to_binary80(value, mode)` for positive, nonzero
normalized `X87Finite` inputs. It computes `E=floor(e/2)`, Euclidean parity
`b=e.rem_euclid(2)`, `N=S << (63+b)`, `q=floor(sqrt(N))`, and exact `u128`
remainder `R=N-q²` for input `x=S*2^(e-63)`. Nearest rounding increments iff
`R>q`; an exact midpoint is impossible. Toward-positive increments iff `R!=0`;
toward-zero and toward-negative do not increment. The rounded significand uses
`u128`, preserving the carry from `u64::MAX` to `2^64` for the existing normal
binary80 packer. Zero, negative and malformed non-normalized values return
`None`.

The reusable `integer_sqrt_u128` and finite sqrt decomposition moved to
`finite_arithmetic.rs`; binary32/binary64 continue to pass the same
exact/nonzero tail representation to their existing packers. Literal raw
10-byte vectors cover the six reviewed `(S,e,E,q,R)` cases in all four modes,
plus exponents `-1`, `-3`, `-16445`, and `16383`, pseudo-denormal equivalence,

## S2-29w — exact finite binary80 scaling to one rounded result

Added `x87::scale_finite_to_binary80(value, power, mode)` for normalized,
nonzero finite binary80 values. For the exact input
`(-1)^sign * S * 2^(e-63)`, it checks normalized finite provenance and `S >=
2^63`, computes `e + power` with checked `i32` addition, forms the exact signed
coefficient `±i128::from(S)`, and calls `round_pack_exact_coefficient` once.
There is no additional shift, GRS arithmetic, or intermediate rounding.

The helper returns `None` only for its bounded rejection cases: zero, malformed
normalization/provenance, checked exponent-add overflow, or a result outside
finite binary80 range. Exact underflow is rounded once and may produce signed
zero, subnormal, or a carry to minimum normal. Inputs remain unchanged;
pseudo-denormal provenance is accepted and output is canonical finite
encoding. This is mathematical helper coverage only, with no FSCALE/FCW/FSW,
guest exception, instruction execution, or physical x86 acceptance claim.

Literal tests cover both signs and all four mathematical rounding modes,
including exact powers, low-significand-bit retention, normal/subnormal
boundaries, pseudo-denormal normalization, minimum-subnormal half/quarter
underflow, raw subnormal significands 3/5/7 scaled by one half, midpoint carry
to minimum normal, max-finite acceptance and doubling rejection, checked
`i32::MIN/MAX` exponent-add overflow versus representable deep underflow,
invalid inputs, and immutability. Expected binary80 bytes are independently
literal. Validation passed: focused `finite_scale` tests 6/6, full
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline` (1,712 passed),
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`,
and `git diff --check`. Graphify was updated after implementation. Independent
`gpt-6.1-sol` high review found three coverage/report corrections; those were
fixed and follow-up review completed cleanly. The layout check passes in the
main checkout; the isolated worktree invocation flags its `.git` pointer and
gitignored oracle manifests absent there. See the [standalone S2-29w report](S2_29W_X87_FINITE_SCALE_BINARY80.md).

ISSUE-019 remains open for broader architectural x87 behavior and physical
acceptance.

## S2-29x — exact truncated finite binary80 remainder decomposition

Added the helper-only `x87::remainder_finite_trunc(lhs, rhs)` returning an exact
`(exponent, coefficient)` decomposition of
`lhs - trunc(lhs / rhs) * rhs`. It accepts normalized nonzero Normal,
Subnormal, and PseudoDenormal values. A negative exponent gap returns the
signed left operand unchanged; gaps from 0 through 64 use an exact `u128`
numerator modulo the right significand; larger gaps and malformed inputs return
`None`. Exact multiples use `(rhs.exponent, 0)` without architectural zero-sign
semantics.

Literal tests cover sign combinations, divisor-sign independence, exact
multiples, the left-smaller path, gap boundaries 0/1/63/64/65, minimum normal
modulo maximum subnormal, raw subnormal 7 modulo 3, pseudo-denormal equivalence,
`i32` exponent endpoints, malformed inputs, and immutability. Independent
literal binary80 bytes verify exact 1.5 and minimum-subnormal remainders in all
four mathematical modes. Focused tests passed 3/3 and the full
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline` passed (1,717 tests). Formatting,
`cargo check -p od-isa --all-targets --offline`, and
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline` passed. Graphify was updated;
independent `gpt-6.1-sol` high review completed with no remaining findings.
The [implementation and three literal unit tests](../../crates/od-isa/src/x87.rs)
include `remainder_finite_trunc` and the signed/gap, provenance/rejection, and
exact-packing compositions.

This is exact finite helper coverage only. No FPREM/FPREM1, partial
reduction/C2, quotient condition bits, FCW/FSW, guest exceptions, architectural
signed-zero behavior, or physical x86 acceptance is claimed. ISSUE-019 remains
open for architectural x87 behavior and physical acceptance. See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-29x-exact-truncated-finite-binary80-remainder-decomposition-bounded-helper),
[CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#local-s2-29x-exact-truncated-finite-binary80-remainder-decomposition),
and [standalone report](S2_29X_X87_FINITE_REMAINDER.md).

Added metadata-returning truncating and nearest-even remainder helpers. Results
preserve the exact remainder pair and expose the integer quotient as a `u128`
magnitude plus separate sign; zero quotient is positive. Nearest-even metadata
reports the rounded integer quotient, while truncation reports the truncated
quotient. The original helpers are projections with unchanged accepted-input
domains and remainder results. Literal tests cover quotient values beyond
`u64`, signed operands, positive zero quotient, both nearest-even tie parities,
exact multiples, negative and maximum positive accepted gaps, malformed and
endpoint exponent inputs, and legacy-wrapper projection/rejection equivalence.
Nearest-even preserves every negative gap: `d <= -2` passes lhs through with
zero quotient, and `d == -1` returns zero for `A <= B` or one for `A > B`.

remainder at the target precision and carry through the existing normal packer.

that differs from p64-then-narrow. The p53 boundary vectors have nonzero exact

## S2-29ab — finite binary80 square-root precision diagnostics

Added `sqrt_finite_to_binary80_precision_with_diagnostics` for positive,
nonzero normalized finite binary80 inputs at p=24/53/64. Its result carries the
raw binary80 value, mathematical `inexact`, and `incremented` (whether the
truncated positive target-precision significand increased by one before carry
normalization). At p64, `inexact` is `R != 0`; at p<64 it is
`L != 0 || R != 0` for exact `(E,q,R)` decomposition and `h=64-p`,
`L=q & ((1<<h)-1)`. This correctly marks exact p24 halfway roots inexact even
when `R=0`. `incremented` and `inexact` are helper-local; neither is
architectural PE/C1.

Both existing bit-only APIs project the `value` field, with the same output
bytes and `None` domains as before. Independent literal bytes and booleans
cover exact roots, all four modes and three precisions, both existing p24
midpoint roots and their expected increment arrays, p53 nonzero-R boundaries,
the p24 direct-rounding versus p64 double-rounding case, carry/exponent cases,
rejections, projection equivalence, and input immutability. See the
[standalone report](S2_29AB_X87_SQRT_DIAGNOSTICS.md) for verification and
review status. No FCW/FSW, exception, decode/execute, native/JIT/C ABI,
physical x86 claim, or common FP diagnostics framework was added. ISSUE-019
remains open.

## S2-31b — bounded `FISTP m32int [RAX]` partial slice

Added only bare `DB 18` as a fixed Dword store through RAX in Long64. The
interpreter preflights existing x87 state, all-masked PC64 FCW, the bounded
FSW mask, old physical TOP Valid tag, canonical-Normal binary80 input, and
unbiased exponent 0..31. It rounds with integer quotient/remainder arithmetic
under the four admitted RC values, rejects signed-i32 overflow before data
access, and encodes negative results with unsigned two's-complement arithmetic.

After the conversion succeeds, the executor validates the entire canonical48
four-byte range, then issues one `write_integer` Dword access with no data read.
The CPU remains unchanged until that write succeeds. Store errors retain their
existing types; an injected architectural #PF remains the memory backend's
reported error, and flat mapping/permission failures are not converted into
guest faults. Successful commit empties old physical TOP, advances TOP, keeps
PE sticky and sets it for a remainder, updates C1 from magnitude increment,
records FIP/FDP, and advances RIP. All x87 raw payload bytes survive.

signed-i32 overflow rejection without data access. Interpreter tests cover the
unaligned exact four-byte store and canaries, no data read, one write, overflow
before access, permission failure atomicity, canonical-range rejection, the
negative i32 minimum, and an injected #PF with unchanged CPU and RAM. The
literal runner test checks split-region output bytes, FSW/TOP/tag/payload/FIP/FDP
state, and no-commit snapshots for invalid tag and overflow. Decoder
enumeration, schema validation, and explicit native denial are included.
The follow-up literal-oracle test runs exact and inexact positive/negative
values through all four RC modes, then checks raw `+2147483647.5` and
`-2147483648.5` binary80 inputs against hand-stated signed-boundary results.
Each success observes FSW in AX through FNSTSW and checks memory bytes; each
rounding-induced overflow verifies zero retirement and no store.

## S2-30an — indexed FCOMI-family register forms

Generalized the four existing `i=1` instructions to all `i=0..7` encodings:

and DF E0 retain their previous operations. Every other DB/DF byte, all legacy
and REX prefixes, WAIT, and memory forms remain rejected. Native execution is
explicitly closed for all four indexed operation variants and all 32 encodings.

Execution reuses `bounded_x87_fcom_result(state, i)`. It validates the x87
snapshot, FCW/FSW, old physical TOP tag and canonical-Normal value. For nonzero
i it also validates the actual physical `(TOP+i)&7` source; for `i=0` it returns

mask `0x8d5`, writes greater/less/equal as zero/CF/ZF, defines all six affected
flags, and clears only FSW.C1. Nonpop forms preserve all tags and TOP. Pop
forms empty old TOP and advance once with wrap, including self compare. Raw
register payloads are preserved; FIP/RIP and retirement update normally.
Rejects remain atomic.

The x87 schema admits exactly 32 comparison instructions, alone or followed
by DF E0 FNSTSW AX: 64 exact strings. It rejects near-miss bytes, prefixes,
memory forms, and excess trailing instructions. Its no-stop/budget-one reject
profile is restricted to a bad actual source with valid old TOP and environment;
i=0 uses the exact all-zero payload class reject. The six new literal CLI
fixtures cover FCOMI self compare at TOP=3 with only TOP Valid; FUCOMIP self
compare/pop at TOP=7 with wrap and only TOP Valid; FUCOMI ST(7) at TOP=7 using
physical slot 6 with old ST(1) Empty; FCOMIP ST(6) at TOP=6 using physical
slot 4 while popping only old TOP; and standalone invalid-source cases for i=0
and i=7 with unrelated ST(1) Valid. Existing i=1 fixtures are unchanged.

<a id="s2-31cl--masked-finite-overflow-to-m64-fistp"></a>

## S2-31cl — masked finite overflow to m64 `FISTP`

Only bare `DF 38` now converts Valid-tagged canonical binary80 Normal inputs
that round outside signed i64. The shared integer converter rounds quotient and
remainder under FCW before comparing the signed bounds. Out-of-range results
store Qword integer-indefinite and add IE only after successful write, clear
C1, and add no PE/OE/UE/DE/SF/ES/B. Values that round back into range retain
finite storage and PE/C1 behavior. Exponent 64+ takes the invalid path without
shifting by a large amount; exponent 63 accepts only exact negative i64
minimum at the lower boundary. Existing fractional behavior below one is
unchanged.

The independent table contains 26 signed literal inputs × four RC modes ×
eight TOPs × incoming IE × incoming PE × incoming C1 (6,656 executions).
Boundary vectors include positive i64 max, its adjacent half-integer and its
neighbor, the negative counterpart, exact i64 min and the next negative
integer. High-exponent vectors cover 64, 65 and 16383 with minimum, mixed and
maximum significands and both signs. Tests also distinguish exact i64 min from
indefinite by IE, prove invalid fractional conversions do not add PE, preserve
raw source bytes and verify denied-write/canonical-range atomicity plus
FNSTSW/FNCLEX.

The formerly rejecting S2-31f positive-overflow fixture is now a literal
`DF 38; DF E0` CLI case: it commits indefinite, pops, observes IE via FNSTSW,
and preserves the source bytes. The CLI fixture and JIT-denial tests passed
1/1 each. The native-denial test is architecture-gated and ran 0 tests on the
local arm64 host; its Linux x86_64 all-target compile succeeded.

<a id="s2-31cr--canonical-subnormal-m16-fist"></a>

## S2-31cr — canonical binary80 subnormals through m16 FIST/FISTP

The bounded DF10/DF18 m16 integer-store path now admits Special-tagged
canonical nonzero binary80 subnormals. It reuses the m32 exact rounding rule:
RN/TZ produce zero; RD produces -1 only for negative input; RU produces +1
only for positive input. Every conversion adds PE and recomputes C1 from the
stored magnitude. The implementation leaves m64 subnormal sources closed and
retains the established FCW/FSW gates, canonical48 Word preflight, one
atomic write/no read, raw binary80 source bytes, and write-before-commit
ordering.

Coverage includes the 65,536-case matrix over four fractions, signs, RC,
FIST/FISTP, TOP, all six incoming sticky flags, and prior C1; FLD m80
composition through both stores with FNSTSW/FNCLEX; malformed/tag/class and
width controls; Word sentinels; and write/range atomicity. A literal
FISTP/FNSTSW fixture verifies negative round-down storage and status
observation. Interpreter success and JIT/native denial are asserted by the
fixture harnesses.

<a id="s2-31cs--canonical-subnormal-m64-fistp"></a>

## S2-31cs — canonical binary80 subnormal through m64 FISTP

Only exact bare `DF 38` now admits Special-tagged canonical binary80
nonzero subnormals (exponent zero, J=0, nonzero fraction). The existing
integer-only conversion helper applies the bounded subnormal result: RN/TZ
store zero, RD stores all-ones only for negative input, and RU stores one only
for positive input. PE is always ORed after a successful Qword write; C1 is
recomputed from whether the rounded magnitude is one. Existing FCW and
`FSW & 0x80c0` gates remain in force, including preservation of all six sticky
flags and C0/C2/C3. `FIST m64` is not introduced. Pseudo-denormals, malformed
encodings, mismatched tags, and unmasked cases remain unsupported.

The 32,768-case ISA matrix uses four literal fractions, both signs, all four
RC values, all eight TOP positions, all 64 incoming IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE
combinations, and both incoming C1 values. It checks literal Qwords, eight-byte
canaries, exactly one Qword write and no read, sticky/condition status
preservation, C1, TOP wrap/pop, FIP/FDP/RIP, and preservation of all raw x87
payloads. Additional checks reject wrong tags, pseudo-denormal, malformed and
zero operands plus disallowed controls/status. Denied writes and canonical48
range failures leave state and RAM unchanged. Existing m16/m32 subnormal
matrix and composition tests remain green.

The literal CLI fixture performs an unaligned `FLD m80`, changes RAX, executes
`FISTP m64`, observes PE/C1 with `FNSTSW AX`, then clears exception flags with
`FNCLEX`. It checks the all-ones Qword between sentinels, the raw popped
subnormal payload, the final TOP/tag/status, and unchanged input bytes. The
fixture schema recognizes only this exact composed byte sequence. JIT
translation and native x86 admission both fail closed for this fixture.

## S2-31di — small canonical-Normal values through bounded FRNDINT

Bare register-only `D9 FC` now admits a Valid canonical-Normal old physical
TOP with unbiased exponent `-16382..=-1`. The comparison-based branch avoids
oversized shifts: nearest-even returns magnitude one only above the exact
halfway significand at `e=-1`; directed modes return one only when sign and
direction move away from zero. Every admitted value adds PE, C1 reports the
magnitude-one choice, and signed zero outputs receive `X87Tag::Zero`. Existing
control/status gates, sticky IE/PE behavior and all unrelated state remain
unchanged.

The local matrix crosses both signs, all four FCWs, all TOPs, `e=-1,-2,-63,
-64,-65,-16382`, three significand patterns, sticky IE/PE combinations and
prior C1. It checks nearest half and adjacent values, values below one,
Valid→Zero/Valid tags, full state preservation, atomic invalid-tag/environment
and execution-boundary rejects, and repeated FRNDINT after rounding to zero.
The literal `s2_31di_frndint_min_normal_to_negative_zero_fnstsw.case.json`
checks minimum-normal input, negative-zero bytes/tag, FNSTSW status, pointer
preservation and retirement. JIT/native denial and no-data-memory behavior
remain covered by existing admission/execution checks. This slice does not
admit subnormal/pseudo-denormal/malformed/tag-mismatched sources or unmasked
exceptions.

The exact Special-tagged branch of bare Long64 `D9 FC` now accepts binary80

SF, ZE, OE or UE. Previously admitted sticky IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE and SF paired

preflight remain unchanged. The result re-enters as the existing QNaN identity;
SNaN quieting remains a distinct path. FLD, classification and JIT/native
admission were not changed.

0/1/bit62/max, sign, all RC modes and TOPs, each legal historical IE/SF
pairing, all prior DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE combinations and C1. It checks full x87/GPR/
RFLAGS canaries and no memory access. Neighbor class/tag, invalid-control and
status rejects plus fetch/truncation/STOP/budget atomicity are covered. A
seeded literal `D9 FC DF E0 DB E2` fixture uses raw Special unnormal input in
the project x87 snapshot, observes AX/FSW `0x4501`, then FNCLEX leaves FSW

native execution.

Normative basis: Intel SDM revision 093 Vol.2A “FRNDINT—Round to Integer,”
p.3-372, lists unsupported format as #IA. Vol.1 Table 8-10 specifies the
masked QNaN floating-point indefinite for an arithmetic operation on an
unsupported format; Table 4-3 and §4.8.3.7 define its binary80 encoding. Table
8-10 gives SNaNs a separate masked response; that behavior is not reused here.
The separate FIST/FISTP denormal #D ambiguity under ISSUE-019 remains unchanged.

### Open x87 denormal question for integer stores

The current canonical-subnormal integer-store slices (`S2-31cq/cr/cs`) expect
PE without newly setting DE. Intel SDM revision 093 Vol.1 §§8.2.2, 8.4.1 and
8.5.2 say pseudo-denormals act as denormal operands, classify FIST/FISTP as
arithmetic, and require #D for an arithmetic denormal operand; the dedicated
Vol.2A FIST/FISTP entry on pp. 3-347–348 lists #IS/#IA/#P but omits #D. The
new-DE behavior is therefore unresolved, not a confirmed implementation bug.
Do not infer hardware behavior from the local PE-only fixtures. ISSUE-019
records a targeted final combined Mac mini check using canonical-subnormal and
pseudo-denormal sources with initial DE=0 through m16/m32 FIST/FISTP and m64
FISTP across RC; compare DE, PE, result, TOP and destination. Defer any FISTP
pseudo-denormal implementation until that question has evidence and a reviewed
contract.

## S2-30bj — narrow bare `FXCH ST(1)`

Implemented exact no-prefix `D9 C9` decode and interpreter semantics. The gate
requires FCW `0x037f`, no FSW bits in `0x80ff`, and Valid-tagged canonical-Normal
values in both physical TOP slots before committing. Success swaps the complete
raw values, preserves their tags and TOP, preserves C0/C2/C3 as a local policy,
clears C1, records FIP, advances RIP by two, and retires once. GPR/RFLAGS/memory
and unrelated x87 payloads remain untouched. No aliases, memory form, stack
underflow, exception delivery, WAIT, JIT lowering, or native acceptance was
added. C0/C2/C3 preservation is deterministic local behavior; no hardware
comparison is claimed for those architecturally undefined fields.

its raw payload and tag, clears C1, updates FIP/RIP and retires. Nonzero forms

C0/C2/C3/FDP/FOP policies remain fixed; no hardware-equivalence claim was
added. No stack exception, new status behavior, JIT or native x87 admission was
introduced.

states with deliberately malformed/Empty nonparticipant canaries, participating

tag, and JIT denial. `cargo test -p od-isa fxch --offline` passed 6/6;
`cargo test -p od-testkit x87_fxch_st1_schema --offline` passed 1/1; focused

## S2-30bm — bounded register-only FINCSTP and FDECSTP

Added exact bare Long64 `D9 F7`/`D9 F6` operations. They update TOP by +1/-1
modulo eight, clear C1, preserve C0/C2/C3 under a deterministic local policy,
and leave every raw x87 register byte and the complete tag word unchanged.
All register contents and tags are opaque: no tag/class reads, reclassification,
exchange, or Empty marking occurs. FIP captures old RIP; FDP/FOP, GPR, RFLAGS,
and memory retain their register-only behavior. The execution gate is present
state, FCW `0x037f`, and `FSW & 0x80ff == 0`.

Coverage includes 1,536 full-state successes (2 directions × 8 TOP values × 16
prior CC states × 6 opaque snapshots), separate TOP wrap, eight repeated
operations, both inverse pairs, all nine forbidden FSW bits, invalid FCW,
missing state, truncated fetch, STOP, zero budget, and adjusted-TOP FXCH
composition. Decoder and schema accept only the exact six requested streams;
four literal runner fixtures seed TOP=7/C1 with distinct raw canaries and mixed
including Empty tags, observe status after each direction, and observe both
inverse orders. JIT denial is asserted. These fixtures and matrices are local
interpreter/schema evidence, not native or physical x86 evidence.

## S2-30bn — bounded FLD1 and FLDZ

The exact bare Long64 forms `D9 E8` and `D9 EE` now push their specified constants only when x87 state is present, FCW is `0x037f`, the masked exception/status environment is clean (`FSW & 0x80ff == 0`), and `(old_TOP+7)&7` is Empty. FLD1 stores exact binary80 one with Valid tag; FLDZ stores exact zero with Zero tag. The implementation preflights before mutation, never reads old Empty payload bytes, updates TOP and clears C1, and records FIP. Other cells/tags and local deterministic undefined fields are preserved. It captures the old source bytes/tag before updating TOP, copies all ten bytes and the tag to the destination, leaves the source in place, clears C1, records FIP, and retires once. Empty destination bytes remain opaque. C0/C2/C3 retention is a local policy without a hardware-equality claim. `D9 C1..C7` remain rejected; no JIT/native acceptance was added.

The 5,120-state full-state interpreter matrix (five magnitudes × two signs × eight TOP values × sixteen prior CC patterns × four snapshots) checks raw bytes, full tags, TOP, C1, pointers, GPR/RFLAGS and canaries. Review follow-up added `Operation::FldSt0` to the native runner's explicit x87-denial match. No Mac mini, SSH, native execution, or physical x86 checks were performed. ISSUE-019 remains open for Empty/Special sources, broader indices, stack exceptions and native/physical acceptance. Implemented exact unprefixed Long64 `DD C0`; all `DD C1..C7` aliases and prefixed forms remain unsupported. The strict gate requires present x87 state, FCW `0x037f`, and `FSW & 0x80ff == 0`. Literal fixtures cover TOP=7/C1=1 mixed canaries with an already-Empty entry, opaque SNaN, the FLD ST(0) Empty rejection, bad environment and `FFREE→FINCSTP→FLD1→FNSTSW` physical-cell reuse. ## S2-19b — bounded `F3 AB` REP STOSW/D/Q (local)

Extended the existing REP STOS operation to word, dword, and qword forms while
keeping exact `F3 AA` byte behavior. Accepted AB prefix forms are F3 with
optional 66, no segment/address override, and absent REX or effective REX.W;
all REX.W values are admitted. Normalization covers `F3 48 66 AB` as word and
`F3 66 48 AB` as qword. All other requested prefix combinations remain
Unsupported, and the native/JIT gate was not expanded.

The loop writes the low accumulator width in one all-or-error store, then
commits DF-directed wrapping RDI and RCX decrement. Zero count avoids access.
Completion is checked before STOP, which is checked before the 1024-successful
store work limit. Partial STOP/limit/fault leaves RIP at the REP start and
retirement zero; earlier successful stores persist. Instruction budget still
counts the completed REP as one instruction. RAX, RSI, RFLAGS and definedness
remain unchanged during one `run()`; definedness resets on a new run.

Added the 12,288-state normal completion matrix, exact prefix and byte boundary
checks, and 28 literal schema-v2 fixtures with full expected-state sidecar.
Fixture generation writes the fixed case constants. ISSUE-016 and ISSUE-020
remain open. Mac mini, SSH, native and physical checks were not run and remain
reserved for final acceptance.

## S2-19c — bounded `F3 AC/AD` REP LODSB/W/D/Q (local)

Added `Operation::RepLods { size }` for exact REP LODSB/W/D/Q profile forms.
Admission accepts exact `F3 AC`, F3 plus optional 66 on `AD`, no segment or
address-size override, and no REX or effective REX.W; every `48..4F` REX.W is
admitted. Normalization yields word for `66 F3 AD` and `F3 48 66 AD`, and qword
for `F3 66 48 AD`. `F3 66 AC`, F2/LOCK/67/segment, non-W REX `AD`, and other
prefixed `AC` forms remain unsupported. Native and JIT do not execute REP
LODS and do not fall back to the interpreter.

Each nonzero iteration reads one width from flat `DS:[RSI]`. Only successful
reads commit the width-selected accumulator alias, DF-directed wrapping RSI
and RCX decrement. Zero count does not read or validate RSI. Completion wins
over STOP; STOP wins over the 1024 successful-read work limit. Partial
STOP/limit leaves RIP on REP and retires zero; read failure preserves prior
completed elements and commits no current-element state. A replay resumes from
that exact RSI/RCX without rereading prior elements. Flags, DF, RDI and RAM do
not change. Missing mapping remains a harness error, no #PF is synthesized,
and no MMIO rollback claim is made. Definedness is checked within a run only;
`run()` reinitializes it on a new invocation.

## S2-19d — bounded `F3 A4/A5` REP MOVSB/W/D/Q (local)

Added `Operation::RepMovs { size }` for exact Long64 forms `F3 A4` byte,
`F3 66 A5` word, `F3 A5` dword and effective REX.W A5 qword. The decoder accepts
all REX.W bytes 48..4F and the specified 66/REX orderings. Segment/address-size
overrides, non-W REX A5, F3 66 A4, conflicting/repeated group prefixes and
other unsupported prefixed A4 forms remain admission failures. Existing
non-REP MOVS, REP STOS and REP LODS remain covered. Native/JIT admission is not
expanded.

The executor reads one width from DS:[RSI], then writes one width to ES:[RDI].
It commits both DF-directed wrapping pointer steps and RCX decrement only
after both accesses succeed. A failed read skips the write; a failed write
follows the successful read without committing the current destination or
register progress. Previously completed transfers persist; replay rereads the
current source. Completion takes priority over STOP and the 1024-success local
limit, and STOP takes priority over that limit. A full REP retires once;
partial fault/STOP/limit keeps the original RIP and retires zero. Zero count
performs no data access even for invalid pointers. This remains a local policy:
no synthetic #PF, MMIO rollback or SMP atomicity claim is made. Flag
definedness is preserved within one run only because a new run reinitializes
the metadata.

also checks zero count with two invalid pointers, page-edge success and

## S2-19e — exact `F3 AE` REPE SCASB (bounded local profile)

data access, even for zero count, it requires arithmetic flag values
`PF|ZF` (`0x44`) and all six arithmetic flags defined (`0x8d5`); DF=0/1 is
allowed. This is a local entry/restart restriction, not an x86 architectural
requirement. Zero count avoids RDI access and preserves flags. For nonzero
count, each read is followed by the existing byte CMP flag calculation, a
wrapping DF-directed RDI update, and RCX decrement. Completion and mismatch
precede STOP and the 1024-success limit; a continuing match checks STOP before
the limit. Faulting iteration state is not committed; prior equal progress
stays in RDI/RCX/flags with RIP at the REP instruction, permitting replay
without hidden state.

## S2-19f — exact `F3 A6` REPE CMPSB (bounded local profile)

The Long64/address64 interpreter now admits only exact `F3 A6`. Before any
data read, including at RCX zero, entry requires arithmetic values `PF|ZF`
(`0x44`) and full arithmetic definedness (`0x8d5`); DF is accepted either way.
This is a local entry/restart restriction, not an architectural REPE CMPS
requirement. With zero count it avoids RSI/RDI validation and data access,
preserves flags, advances RIP by two, and retires once.

Each nonzero iteration reads source DS:[RSI], then destination ES:[RDI], and
uses the existing CMP calculation for source minus destination. Only after both
reads succeed does it commit flags, wrapping RSI/RDI by DF and RCX decrement.
Completion/mismatch precedes STOP and the 1024-success limit; STOP precedes
the limit. A first-read failure skips the second access. A second-read failure
leaves its first read visible but commits none of the current iteration. Prior
equal iterations persist and retry rereads both values; no pending source is
stored. This source-first order is local policy only, recorded in ISSUE-020;
MMIO rollback is not claimed. Mappings/backend errors remain harness errors.

computing CPU results. Fixture tests compare complete interpreter snapshots and

## S2-19g — bounded `F3 AF` REPE SCASW/D/Q

The Long64/address64 decoder and interpreter now admit normalized group1 F3
with AF as SCASW (`F3 66 AF`), SCASD (`F3 AF`), or SCASQ using effective
REX.W. Prefix order is significant: `F3 48 66 AF` is SCASW because the later
legacy 66 discards the earlier REX, while `F3 66 48 AF` is SCASQ because the
final REX.W is effective. Every `48..4F` REX.W byte is accepted when effective.
Prefix/width admission rejects the exact requested invalid set;
`F3 AE` remains byte-only and `F3 66 AE` remains Unsupported. The existing
arithmetic entry/restart gate still runs before all reads, including RCX zero.
It requires concrete `PF|ZF` values and definedness `ARITHMETIC_FLAGS`; this is
the local profile restriction, not an architectural REPE requirement.

SCASW/D/Q compare AX/EAX/RAX with a width-sized read at flat `ES:[RDI]`. The
existing width-aware SCAS loop commits flags, wrapping DF-directed RDI and
RCX only after a successful read; it preserves complete RAX, RSI, RAM and
non-arithmetic flags. Completion/mismatch precede STOP and the iteration cap;
matching continuation checks STOP before the 1024-success cap. Fault, STOP and
limit preserve REP RIP and do not retire. Replay re-enters the same gate, and
equal progress retains `PF|ZF` with full arithmetic definedness.

Coverage includes 864 single-comparison states, 720 termination paths,
49,140 W/D/Q gate rejections plus the retained 16,380 byte gate cases, 72
injected width read failures, 12 STOP/replay paths, 18 width limit cases,
mismatch-at-1024/STOP/limit ordering, initial STOP, budget zero, RCX maximum,
zero count with invalid RDI, unaligned/range/wrap and noncanonical
post-index cases. Exactly 59 schema-v2 fixtures compare complete state and
memory. The CLI fixture test requires JIT Unsupported with no interpreter
fallback for every case; a Linux-only native admission test covers each width
and both normalized prefix orders. The native test could not execute on this
macOS host because `native_v2` is gated to Linux x86_64. No Mini, SSH, native
execution, or physical acceptance was run.

## S2-18o — non-REP address-size-32 MOVS

Added 73 literal schema-v2 fixtures for the bounded `67 A4`, `67 66 A5`,
`67 A5`, and `67 48 A5` forms: 8 successes, 8 unmapped errors, 4 read-only
destination errors, 4 zero-budget cases, 16 pointer wraps, 6 continuous spans
across 4 GiB, 2 prefix normalizations, 3 TEST compositions, 8 CLD/STD
compositions, 4 aliases, 4 dual-invalid cases, and 6 partial overlaps. One
positive case pairs a read-only source with a write-only destination. Literal
full-state answers are in `s2_18o_movs_addr32_expected.json`; the committed
`s2_18o_movs_addr32_manifest.json` is authoritative for hashes and exact
inventory.

The local executor reads the complete source before writing the destination;
overlap therefore uses pre-write source bytes. Address-size-32 truncates only

### S2-19j correction — address-size-32 count uses ECX

Review found that the original executor and report incorrectly used the full
RCX for S2-19j count checks and decrements. Intel SDM Vol. 1 REP pseudocode
selects ECX when address-size is 32 and performs the decrement inside
`WHILE CountReg != 0`: ECX=0 therefore performs no iteration and leaves the
entire RCX unchanged. After a successful iteration, the 32-bit ECX decrement
zero-extends into RCX. The implementation, contract, plan, interpreter test
guide, fixture provenance, and the original “decrements RCX” claim are corrected
to state these effects.

Two new literal schema-v2 fixtures cover zero instruction budget and STOP at
the initial RIP with nonzero RCX high-half and ECX=0; all nine S2-19j fixture
cases now carry nonzero RCX high-half where appropriate. Unit coverage checks
successful ECX=1→0, ECX>1 partial progress and resumed completion, no mutation
for zero count/budget/initial STOP, and a read fault after a committed element.
The address-size-64 REP LODS and existing REP LODS matrices continue to pass.
No opcode forms or fixture schema/profile were added.

Verification: targeted `od-isa` address-size-32 tests passed 4/4 and the
`od-testkit` literal fixture test passed 1/1; `cargo test --workspace --offline`
passed; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `cargo fmt --all
-- --check`, S2-19j generator freshness and `git diff --check` passed. Graphify
was updated. No native/JIT, Mac mini, SSH or physical x86 validation was run.
ISSUE-022 records this corrected semantic defect as resolved; ISSUE-016/020/021
remain open and outside this change. Independent gpt-6.1-sol high review found
no code or fixture defects; it identified one stale paragraph in
`docs/testing/INTERPRETER.md`, which was corrected to the same ECX semantics and
nine-fixture count before review closed.

## S2-19m — bounded REPE SCASB address-size-32

which precedes the 1024-success cap; fault/STOP/limit leave REP RIP and retire
zero. Tracked resume carries the prior definedness mask.

generic SCAS loop was sufficient: it already selects ECX/EDI, performs one
width-sized read, and commits the current iteration only after a successful
read. This does not claim that a read wraps at 4 GiB; a cross-boundary operand
is one contiguous width-sized access.

defined, even when ECX is zero. Zero count performs no data access and preserves
the full state. Nonzero success compares AX/EAX/RAX and commits flags, modulo-32
EDI and zero-extended ECX-1. Completion/mismatch precedes STOP and the 1024-read
limit. Fault, STOP and limit preserve REP RIP and do not retire; prior successful
iterations remain committed. JIT/native remain closed. ISSUE-020 remains open.

restart behavior; local fault handling does not claim physical #PF semantics.

## S2-34.2 — local register MOVUPS slice

Added separate schema-v2 profile `s2-long-movups-reg-v1`; the S2-34.1
`s2-long-x87-sse-state-v1` profile remains NOP-only. The new profile admits
one legacy `0F 10 /r` with ModR/M.mod=3, optionally preceded by one effective
REX. REX.R/B select the XMM register indices. REX.W/X are excluded, as are
legacy `66`, F2/F3, segment/address, LOCK and duplicate/ignored-prefix
variants, memory forms, `0F 11`, SSE2 alternatives, VEX and EVEX. The form was
checked against Intel SDM version 093, Vol. 2B, MOVUPS entry `0F 10 /r` and its
ModR/M operand encoding; the separate `0F 11 /r` store form is not included.

The diagnostic profile assumes SSE availability, CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and
CR4.OSFXSR=1. It does not implement control registers, `#UD/#NM`, memory or
alignment behavior, MXCSR effects, floating-point arithmetic, native/JIT or
physical x86 execution. A successful operation copies all 128 source bits,
including self-copy, while preserving x87, MXCSR, GPR and RFLAGS. RIP and
retirement advance only after successful execution. Decoder matrices cover all
256 XMM source/destination pairs across REX.R/B; literal fixture/runner tests
cover XMM8←XMM9 and snapshot preservation; negative cases cover prefix,
ModR/M and truncation rejection. Native profile admission explicitly denies
the profile. This is local completion only; S2-34/D/System remains open.

## S2-34.4 — local MOVUPS memory-source load from `[RAX]`

Added a new schema-v2 profile, `s2-long-movups-mem-load-v1`; the S2-34.1
state-only profile remains NOP-only and the S2-34.2/.3 register profile remains
register-only. The profile admits exactly legacy `0F 10 /r` with
ModR/M.mod=00, r/m=000, optionally preceded by one effective REX.R for the
destination. REX.B/X/W, SIB, displacement, other bases, `0F 11`, legacy prefix
variants, duplicate prefixes, VEX and EVEX fail closed. The encoding follows
Intel SDM revision 093, Vol. 2B, MOVUPS `0F 10 /r`, Op/En RM.

Execution checks the full 16-byte canonical48 range for `[RAX]`, performs one
`GuestMemory::read` into a temporary 16-byte array, then updates only the
selected XMM register and RIP. It does not model this width as `OperandSize::Qword`.
The unaligned fixture loads bytes `00` through `0f` from a read-only region at
RAX=`0x200001`, preserving surrounding canaries, source memory, every other XMM,
x87, MXCSR, GPR and RFLAGS. Local tests cover all 16 destinations, byte patterns
with both high and low bits set, exact one-read/no-write callback traces, first
and last canonical boundaries, cross-hole and u64-overflow rejection, injected
read/backend/fetch failure no-commit, and forbidden encoding variants. The
native runner explicitly denies the profile; its Linux-target test code was
compile-checked, not run on a Linux host. The local CLI fixture also explicitly
denies JIT without interpreter fallback.

## S2-34.5 — local MOVUPS memory store to `[RAX]`

Added separate profile `s2-long-movups-mem-store-v1`; the prior state-only,
register, and memory-load profiles retain their contracts. It admits only
legacy `0F 11 /r`, ModR/M.mod=00, r/m=000 (`[RAX]`), with optional effective
REX.R selecting source XMM0–15. Intel SDM revision 093, Vol. 2B, MOVUPS
`NP 0F 11 /r`, Op/En B (`xmm2/m128, xmm1`) defines XMM as source and memory as
destination. The SDM allows unaligned memory operands, lists no SIMD FP
exceptions and defers other exceptions to Type 4 with a note that #AC treatment
varies; this slice implements no architectural control gates or exceptions.

The executor validates all 16 bytes in the canonical48 diagnostic model,
captures raw `[u8; 16]` from the selected XMM before backend access, issues one
`GuestMemory::write`, and commits RIP/retirement only after success. It issues
no read and does not use `OperandSize::Qword`. Injected backend write failures
leave CPU state unchanged. FlatMemory separately documents/tests all-or-error
for its private synchronous fixture RAM, with no hardware 16-byte atomicity,
MMIO or SMP claim. Upper-u64 overflow remains the explicit ISSUE-012
restriction. A handwritten full-state literal, all 16 XMM source test vectors,
canaries, unaligned address, one-write/no-read trace, permission/mapping/backend
failures, canonical/overflow boundaries, forbidden/truncated encodings,
STOP/budget behavior and JIT/native denial cover the bounded slice. S2-34/D/System
remain open. x86-64-v1 is only an ABI floor; this slice does not complete a
generic CPU profile. ## S2-34.6a — local MOVUPS base+displacement memory forms

Added separate profile `s2-long-movups-mem-base-v1` for both legacy

base GPR and absent/signed disp8/signed disp32. REX.R extends XMM selection;
REX.B extends the GPR base. SIB, mod=00/rm=101 RIP-relative, REX.W/X,
address-size 32, segment/other legacy prefixes, VEX and EVEX remain Unsupported.

admissions. Encoding was checked against Intel SDM revision 093 Vol. 2B MOVUPS
and Vol. 2A §§2.1.3–2.1.5, 2.2.1.1–2.2.1.3 ([official SDM page](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html),

full 16-byte range through the shared helper; loads read once into a temporary
before XMM/RIP commit, and stores capture raw XMM bytes before one write and
advance RIP only after success. Backend errors preserve full CPU state.

hardware atomicity. Default DS/SS and #SS/#GP attribution come from
`MemoryOperand`; RBP is SS-attributed and R13 data-attributed. RSP/R12 require
SIB and cannot be encoded in this no-SIB slice. ISSUE-012's upper-u64
AddressOverflow behavior remains open. The literal fixture exercises
`MOVUPS [R8-7],XMM8`; executor tests exercise both directions, low/high XMM,
supported base classes, signed displacement extrema, exact one-callback
accesses, canonical-range faults, backend no-commit, STOP/budget and forbidden
or truncated encodings. Native/JIT and physical execution remain excluded.

fixtures cover XMM8 load/store, unaligned data, and canaries. Tests cover both
directions with positive/zero/negative disp32, 7/8-byte lengths, current-RIP
and unsigned-disp discriminators, high-XMM selection, exact one-callback access,
canonical crossing, injected backend no-commit, all four disp32 truncations,
STOP/budget and unsupported SIB/prefix/REX.B forms. Earlier state/register/

## S2-34.6c — shared SIB-addressed MOVUPS memory forms

Extended the existing local-only `s2-long-movups-mem-base-v1` profile to
legacy `0F 10 /r` loads and `0F 11 /r` stores through SIB addressing with
64-bit address size. Intel SDM revision 093 Vol. 2A §§2.1.3–2.1.5 and
2.2.1.1–2.2.1.3 establishes SIB scale, REX extensions, and the special
`mod=00/base=5` no-base disp32 form. `index=4` means no index with REX.X=0 and
R12 with REX.X=1. REX.B does not change `mod=00/base=5`; `mod=01/10` can select
R13. Intel SDM Vol. 1 §§3.3.7.1, 3.7.4.1, 3.7.5.1 confirms #SS attribution
for actual RSP/RBP base references; R12/R13 base and index-only/no-base forms
remain DS/#GP attributed. References:
[official Intel SDM page](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html),
[Vol. 2A PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199),
[Vol. 2B PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf),
[Vol. 1 PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436).

The decoder reuses `rm_operand`/`MemoryOperand`; execution reuses the existing
full-range 16-byte validation and generic one-read/one-write path. Loads remain
temporary-before-commit, stores capture source bytes before writing, and any
backend error leaves CPU state uncommitted. Flat fixture RAM all-or-error does
not imply hardware atomicity, MMIO behavior or SMP ordering. Two handwritten
schema-v2 fixtures cover a scaled RSP-based load and no-base R12-index store;
runner snapshots verify state/memory/canaries and retain native/JIT denial.
The local matrix covers scale 1/2/4/8, absent/normal/R12 index, RSP/RBP/R12/R13
and no-base, REX.B/X, mod 00/01/10 displacements, both opcodes, all XMM
registers, callback width, canonical #SS/#GP attribution, failures, truncation,
prefix rejection, and STOP/budget. REX.W, address-size 32, legacy segment or
mandatory prefixes, VEX/EVEX, alignment/control gates and native/JIT execution
remain unsupported. S2-34 remains open and x86-64-v1 remains only the ABI
floor.

## S2-34.8b — local reverse-direction register MOVSS slice

legacy register-operation pseudocode copies bits 31:0 and leaves destination
bits 127:32 unmodified ([official Volume 2B PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf),
pp. 4-118–4-119; [Intel manual page](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html)).
F3 is the mandatory opcode prefix here, not REP: RCX and DF are independent,
and this register form performs no data-memory callbacks.

callback absence, truncated fetch, STOP/budget, strict schema rejection of the

permutations/W/X, VEX and EVEX. The literal `F3 45 0F 11 C1` fixture checks
XMM8→XMM9 with asymmetric low and preserved high bits. Existing MOVSS load,
MOVUPS, logic SSE and REP tests were not changed in behavior. Native/JIT,
feature gates, exception delivery, and physical CPU execution are not claimed.

## S2-35.22 — local PCMPGTW XMM register slice

Added strict `s2-long-pcmpgtw-reg-v1` for legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F 65 /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, with ModR/M.reg as the
XMM destination and ModR/M.r/m as source. Eight independent little-endian i16
lanes write `FFFF` only when signed destination is strictly greater than
signed source; otherwise they write `0000`. Only destination XMM and RIP change.
SSE2/CR0/CR4 preconditions are assumptions; no feature-gate or exception
delivery claim is made. PCMPGTD/Q, memory/MMX, other comparisons, extra
prefixes, REX.W/X, VEX/EVEX, native/JIT and physical execution are excluded.

their in-range neighbors, then against each lhs's in-range signed predecessor,
equal value and successor using an independent i32 oracle. Explicit
destination/source and strict/equality cases, word-vs-byte sentinels
(`0100>00ff`, `0080>007f`), mixed lanes, the full 16×16 XMM/REX matrix,
complete state/flags/MXCSR preservation, and zero data callbacks are checked.
Missing state, truncation and STOP/budget failures are atomic. Strict
schema/decoder negatives include VEX `C5 F9 65 C1`. A handwritten literal
XMM8/XMM9 fixture verifies mixed output, interpreter execution, and JIT/native
denial.

little-endian i16 words from the original destination and source, clamps each
through a widened signed value to [0,255], and writes eight destination bytes
followed by eight source bytes. Only the destination XMM register and RIP change;
a distinct source register and all other architectural state are preserved.
Self-pack reads the original aliased value before writing. SSE2 and CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1 remain assumptions only.
JIT compilation and native execution are denied.

Coverage includes `ffff` (-1), `8000`, `ff00`, and boundary inputs
0000/0001/007f/0080/00ff/0100/7fff; an independent two's-complement widened
reference checks every i16 bit pattern at each of eight lanes in each operand.
The suite also covers all 16×16 XMM/REX.R/B pairs, destination-then-source
ordering, self-aliasing, full-state and source preservation, zero data-memory
callbacks, truncation, missing SSE state, STOP/budget atomicity, strict schema
and decoder negatives including VEX `C5 F9 67 C1`, and a handwritten literal
XMM8/XMM9 fixture. JIT denial is exercised by the fixture runner, and native
denial is covered by the Linux-gated admission test (compile-checked here, not
executed on this Darwin host).

`cargo test -p od-isa packuswb --offline`, `cargo test -p od-testkit packuswb
--offline`, and `cargo test -p od-runner packuswb_literal_fixture --offline`
passed. The complete `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline --quiet`
run passed. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, host
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, Linux x86_64
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline --target
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `git diff --check` passed. `graphify update .`

## S2-34.22 — local MOVUPD `[RAX],XMM` store profile

Added an independent schema-v2 local profile for exact `66 [REX.R] 0F 11 /r`
with memory operand `[RAX]` and source XMM0–15. It copies the source into a
16-byte temporary, performs one 16-byte write and advances RIP only on success;
there are no data-memory reads. Unaligned addresses are accepted locally. The
contract does not claim hardware atomicity, MMIO/SMP behavior, `#AC`, fault
priority, or rollback for arbitrary memory backends. JIT/native admission stays
denied; the handwritten fixture is XMM8 and writable data. Parent S2-34 remains
open; physical execution is `not_run`; ISSUE-012 remains open.

## S2-34.23 — local MOVUPD base+displacement memory profile

Callback tests confirm one 16-byte data callback per operation; injected load and store failures preserve CPU state.

## S2-34.24 — local MOVUPD RIP-relative memory profile

Added a separate strict profile `s2-long-movupd-mem-rip-v1` for long-mode mandatory-66 MOVUPD load/store with ModRM.mod=00/rm=101 and signed disp32. It admits no REX or REX.R only (bytes `40`/`44`); REX.B is rejected, never interpreted as R13. XMM register selection uses ModRM.reg plus REX.R. Effective address is next RIP after the entire instruction plus sign-extended disp32; lengths are 8/9 bytes without/with REX. `rm_operand` and the existing `NextRip`/16-byte memory path are reused. Old `[RAX]` and base+displacement profiles remain strict; base-profile schema validation independently rejects RIP-relative encodings, including mapped-target disp32.

Handwritten load/store fixtures use mapped data and XMM8/REX.R; runner checks literal XMM payloads, stored bytes and canaries, interpreter retirement, and JIT denial. Decoder/execution unit matrices cover both directions and all 16 XMM registers, absent/REX.R 8/9-byte lengths, signed disp32 extrema/negative/zero/positive offsets, exact callback addresses and 16-byte widths, canonical crossing, truncated fetch, zero budget and stop-before-fetch. Testkit callback/error checks verify one 16-byte access and CPU-state preservation. Schema negatives reject REX.B/X/W, SIB/base forms, wrong opcode/prefix, address-size 32, VEX/EVEX and truncation; old `[RAX]` and base profiles reject mapped-target RIP independently. Existing MOVUPS RIP load/store fixtures remain valid after narrowing the schema-only MOVUPD profile gate.

Verification: `cargo test -p od-isa movupd --offline` (16), `cargo test -p od-testkit movupd_memory_base --offline` (2), three focused MOVUPD runner tests and both MOVUPS RIP regression tests passed; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, workspace offline all-target check, Linux x86-runner all-target compile check, `git diff --check` and `graphify update .` passed. Native denial was compile-checked only. SSE2/control-state preconditions are assumed; no hardware alignment/fault, arbitrary-backend rollback, or physical execution claim is made. Parent S2-34 remains open, ISSUE-012 remains open, and physical status is `not_run`. See [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#local-profile-s2-3424-s2-long-movupd-mem-rip-v1), [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-3424-local-movupd-rip-relative-diagnostic-profile).

## S2-35.52 — local PAVGB register profile

Added local-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-pavgb-reg-v1` for the exact
long-mode XMM register encoding `66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F E0 /r`,
ModR/M.mod=3. Mandatory `66` keeps the MMX form outside the profile; REX.R/B
independently select all 16 XMM registers. The interpreter computes each
unsigned byte lane as `(old_DEST + old_SRC + 1) >> 1` in a `u16` intermediate,
snapshots the source for aliasing, preserves all unrelated CPU state, and makes
no data-memory callback. SSE2 and CR0/CR4 requirements remain assumed
preconditions; feature gates, guest exception delivery, JIT/native support,
and physical execution are not claimed. Semantics are from Intel SDM revision
093, Vol. 2B, PAVGB/PAVGW ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf)).

Handwritten fixture `s2_35_52_pavgb_register.case.json` executes
`PAVGB XMM8,XMM9` and records XMM8 result
`88898a8b8c8d8e8f9091929394959697`. Decoder and execution tests cover all
16×16 register pairs, lane-varying inputs, rounding boundaries, aliasing,
full-state preservation, and no memory callbacks. Negative tests reject MMX,
PAVGW, memory, extra prefixes, REX.W/X, VEX/EVEX and truncation; missing SSE
state and incomplete fetch remain atomic. Testkit enforces the exact schema
profile; CLI interpreter accepts the fixture and JIT denies it. Native runner
denial is Linux-only and was compile-checked on this macOS host, not executed.

## S2-37e / bounded S2-38a — local MINSS masked IE/DE status

Implemented the local-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-minss-reg-masked-v1` for
exactly `F3 [optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5D /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, XMM0–15 in
Long64. The profile requires SSE state, all six MXCSR exception masks set,
DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved MXCSR bits 16–31 clear. Any RC and pre-set sticky
flags are permitted. Unsupported state is refused locally and does not claim
architectural #GP/#XM/#UD delivery.

The executor snapshots both low dwords before mutation. Either QNaN or SNaN
selects operand 2 and sets IE sticky. With DAZ clear, a subnormal in the same
operation adds DE only when invalid is not raised; prior DE remains sticky. Non-NaN values use the existing `Binary32::min_sse_raw_result`
selection semantics, including operand-2 selection for equal values and signed
zeros. Only the destination low dword and MXCSR IE/DE bits change; the upper
destination 96 bits and every other state bit are preserved. Aliasing is
supported and no data-memory callback occurs. JIT, native and CPUID admission
remain closed.

The handwritten fixture `s2_37e_minss_masked_register.case.json` exercises
XMM8←XMM9 QNaN plus smallest positive subnormal, selecting RHS and producing
MXCSR `0x1f81` because invalid has priority over same-operation denormal.
Tests cover all 256 register pairs, QNaN/SNaN in either
position, signed-zero orderings, subnormal/NaN combinations, all RC encodings,
sticky preservation, invalid-MXCSR and missing-SSE atomic refusals, exact
decoder negatives/truncation/no-memory behavior, fixture literals, and explicit
JIT/native denial.

Normative sources are Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 §11.5 and Appendix D Tables D-9
and D-15 (masked exception and denormal status), and Vol. 2B `MINSS` (operand
selection). This is only the masked IE/DE subset consumed by S2-37e. Full
unmasked exception delivery, #XM, CR0/CR4/OSXMMEXCPT gating, memory/alignment/FP
fault priority and ordering, and the rest of S2-38 remain open. The Linux
native-denial path is compile-checked only. All Mac mini/physical validation is
deferred to the combined final hardware substage.

## S2-38a follow-up — masked MIN/MAX same-operation exception priority

A correctness review of the committed S2-37e/f/g/h/i masked-status profiles
found that the first implementation added DE for a subnormal even when the
same scalar operation/lane also raised higher-priority IE for a NaN. Intel SDM
Rev. 093 Vol. 1 §4.9.2 ranks invalid/QNaN handling above denormal and permits a
masked lower-priority exception to be ignored; §11.5.2 applies this precedence
to SIMD operations. Appendix D Tables D-9/D-13 specify raw-RHS NaN selection
and invalid status for MIN/MAX. For packed operations, §11.5.3.1 ORs the
per-operation status, so distinct lanes can still contribute IE and DE.

The executor now computes `lane_ie = result.invalid_operation()` and adds DE
for that lane only when `lane_ie` is false and either input is subnormal. Scalar
MINSS/MAXSS/MINSD use the same priority. This suppresses only new DE for a
same-operation NaN lane; prior IE does not suppress DE, prior DE remains sticky,
and separate packed lanes can set both IE and DE.

Updated the MINSS and MINSD literal expectations from MXCSR `0x1f83` to
`0x1f81`. MINPS/MAXPS fixtures now put a subnormal without NaN in one lane and
QNaN plus subnormal in another, exercising IE|DE aggregation across lanes.
Focused packed unit tests with no independent subnormal lane verify same-lane
suppression. Scalar literal vectors, all-register-pair oracles, packed lane
aggregation and sticky-bit tests cover the corrected rule.
The fixture provenance, fixture README, test format, interpreter guide, CPU
contract and S2-38a plan description were corrected. No new known issue remains
from this repaired finding.

**Repair checks:** `cargo test -p od-isa --offline register_masked` passed
(20 tests), `cargo test -p od-isa --offline scalar_minmax_prioritizes_new_flags_and_preserves_old_sticky_status`
passed (1 test), `cargo test -p od-testkit --offline` passed (369 tests), the
masked runner fixtures passed (5 tests), and the unrelated MOVSD fixture
regression passed (1 test). `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, the Linux
`od-x86-runner --all-targets` cross-check, `git diff --check`, and `graphify
update .` passed. Independent Sol medium code review found no remaining

No physical Mac mini result is claimed; those checks remain grouped in the final

## S2-37j / bounded S2-38a — local MAXSD masked IE/DE status

Added local-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-maxsd-reg-masked-v1` for exactly
one Long64 `F2 [optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5F /r` instruction, ModR/M.mod=3,
XMM0–15. The decoder now globally distinguishes F2 MAXSD from F3 MAXSS and
bare MAXPS. Strict profile validation accepts only this MAXSD shape, and the
existing MINSD profile continues to reject it at the profile layer. Memory,
repeated/misplaced prefixes, REX.W/X, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX remain closed.

Execution snapshots only source and destination low qwords and calls the
existing `Binary64::max_sse_raw_result`. The result commits only the
destination low qword; the upper qword and unrelated state are preserved.
Same-operation priority is `lane_ie = result.invalid_operation()` followed by
`lane_de = !lane_ie && (either low operand is subnormal)`, then OR into the old
MXCSR sticky status. Thus same-lane NaN plus subnormal adds IE without new DE;
old DE remains set, and old IE does not suppress a new DE. High-qword NaN and
subnormal sentinels are ignored. SSE presence and masked MXCSR preconditions
are enforced before mutation; JIT/native/CPUID, memory and unmasked fault paths
remain closed.

status and upper-qword preservation. Decoder and executor tests cover all 256

old IE/DE sticky combinations, upper-qword isolation and atomic refusals. Runner
tests check strict neighboring-form rejection and JIT denial; the native runner
fixture-denial list includes MAXSD. No physical or Mac mini execution was run;
it remains in the combined final hardware substage.

## S2-39a — legacy FXSAVE/FXRSTOR contract (evidence only)

FTW/TOP rotation, XMM0–15, MXCSR mask fallback, alignment and architectural
gate/fault preconditions in the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-39a--legacy-fxsavefxrstor-contract-evidence-only). The exact Ubuntu 7.0.0-38.38 static
package evidence ties the mask probe `0F AE 05 6B F9 17 00` to plain
`FXSAVE` RIP+disp32, and the save/restore forms `48 0F AE 40 40` and
`48 0F AE 4B 40` to `FXSAVE64`/`FXRSTOR64`; details and source locations are in
the [Linux profile report](STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-39a--fxsave-evidence-only).

This documentation-only slice adds no implementation or executable checks and
does not claim a boot, C/D acceptance, physical execution, or whole-area
atomicity. The chosen generic `amd64` target is selected, but target
implementation, runtime manifest and boot remain open. S2-39b has resolved

are still not the FXSAVE memory image. The recommended initial
implementation is the exact RIP-relative mask-probe FXSAVE form once the
required architectural state fields are represented and its memory effects
are implemented. FXSAVE writes defined
state in the 512-byte area, while preserving software-available bytes 464–511;
reserved bytes 416–463 are not treated as meaningful state or given write
semantics here. Mac mini/SSH checks stay in the combined final hardware
substage.

## S2-39b — selector state representation only

Added independently optional `instruction_selector: Option<u16>` and
`data_selector: Option<u16>` to `X87State`, plus matching optional hexadecimal
fields in strict schema-v2 `X87Snapshot`. Missing values serialize absent;
`Some(0)` remains distinct from unavailable. The existing 64-bit FIP/FDP
fields are unchanged. Fixture seeds and all prior profiles leave selectors
absent; profile validation rejects supplied selectors outside the new profile.
The whole `X87Snapshot` comparison already compares both presence and value.

Added `s2-long-x87-selectors-state-v1`, requiring x87, SSE and both selectors.
It admits exactly the one-byte NOP with instruction budget 1 and stop RIP after
that byte. The handwritten fixture uses distinct nonzero selectors, high-width
pointer sentinels, mixed raw x87 registers, physical tag word `0xe4e4`, TOP=3,
opcode, and all XMM/MXCSR state.
Interpreter NOP preserves all represented x87 and SSE fields. The C fragment
adapter rejects the containing x87 state; JIT and native execution remain
unsupported. Existing supported x87 instructions fail closed before their
semantic state mutation or data-memory access whenever either selector is
present, because their FCS/FDS transitions are not modeled. No selector is
inferred from CS/DS. Existing STOP-address and zero-budget ordering is
unchanged.

This closes ISSUE-026 for representation only. It does not implement FNINIT,
FXSAVE/FXRSTOR, a 512-byte memory image, guest exception delivery, native
observation, boot, or physical behavior. Plain Long64 REX.W=0 forms remain
unsupported; S2-39 remains open. Physical/Mac mini work remains in the combined
final hardware substage.

## S2-39c — plain Long64 RIP-relative FXSAVE

Added the strict local profile `s2-long-fxsave-rip-v1` for exactly one
unprefixed `0F AE 05 disp32` Long64 instruction. It requires x87/SSE state and

unsupported; the exact S2-39e restore is documented separately below. CPUID FXSR, CR0.EM/TS=0
and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are selected-target preconditions, not runtime gates in the
current state model. CPUID execution, JIT and native admission remain closed.

The interpreter writes FCW/FSW, abridged physical FTW, masked 11-bit FOP,
low 32-bit FIP/FDP plus independent selectors, raw MXCSR, the immutable target
mask `0x0000_ffbf`, TOP-rotated raw 80-bit stack payloads and raw XMM0–15.

synthetic Generic amd64 target and remains separate from the testkit diagnostic
mask despite equal current values. `state.mxcsr` is not masked.

The local preflight checks alignment and the complete canonical48 512-byte
range before writes; it is a local profile constraint and does not claim

cover `[0,5)`, `[6,14)`, `[16,22)`, `[24,32)`, eight 10-byte stack slots, and
`[160,416)`. All holes remain intact. Intel explicitly requires preservation
of bytes 464–511; preserving reserved bytes is a local policy. On callback
failure, prior private synchronous RAM writes remain, the failed slice is
unchanged under the GuestMemory callback contract, later callbacks stop, and
CPU/RIP/retirement do not commit. This does not promise whole-area rollback,
MMIO behavior, or shared-DMA/SMP guarantees.

The observed literal fixture `0F AE 05 6B F9 17 00` and an independent second

both selectors including zero, high pointer truncation, raw MXCSR and target

negatives, fetch truncation, STOP/zero-budget, runner JIT rejection and native

## S2-39d — exact Long64 FXSAVE64 `[RAX+0x40]`

Added a separate `s2-long-fxsave64-rax-disp8-v1` profile for exactly the
five-byte encoding `48 0F AE 40 40`. It requires the 512-byte destination at
aligned canonical `RAX+0x40`, x87/SSE state, budget 1, and stop RIP immediately
after the instruction. The decoder rejects other REX/prefix, base register,
ModRM, displacement and FXRSTOR64 forms. JIT/native admission remains closed.

The existing FXSAVE serializer now takes an explicit plain or Long64 image
layout. Plain S2-39c remains unchanged: it still requires known FCS/FDS and
writes low 32-bit FIP/FDP with selector fields. FXSAVE64 does not require or
mutate selectors; it writes full 64-bit FIP at `[8,16)` and FDP at `[16,24)`.
Both layouts use the same 13 ascending write-only callbacks, with the two
pointer callback lengths changing from 8/6 to 10/8 bytes. All other saved
fields, target MXCSR mask, TOP-rotated raw ST slots, XMM0–15 and preserved
sentinels share the established S2-39c path.

The handwritten fixture uses exact observed bytes, absent selectors, high-width
distinct pointers and an `A5`-filled destination. Focused tests cover exact
prefix-stream decoding/truncation, selectors absent and present (including
independent availability), all TOP values, pointer bytes, and callback
order/count. Callback failure at every write confirms earlier slices remain
committed, the failing and later slices stay untouched, and CPU/RIP/retirement
do not commit. Profile and execution regressions confirm a wrapping `RAX+0x40`
effective address can select canonical image address zero, while canonical
range and overflow preflight remain enforced. The runner CLI confirms
interpreter success with JIT and native-x86 denial. Existing plain FXSAVE and
MFENCE tests remain passing. These are local interpreter/profile results only;
no hardware/physical, guest exception-delivery, FXRSTOR, or round-trip result is
claimed. Mac mini checks remain grouped in the final hardware substage.

**Checks:** `od-isa` FXSAVE64 tests (3/3), FXSAVE regressions (6/6), and MFENCE
regression (1/1) passed. `od-testkit` FXSAVE64 profile/execution tests (2/2)
and literal fixture execution (2/2, including wrapped effective address) passed.
The `od-runner` FXSAVE64 CLI interpreter/JIT/native test passed. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`,
`cargo check -p od-x86-runner --all-targets --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --offline`,
`git diff --check`, and `graphify update .` passed. The Linux target check is
compile-only on this Apple ARM host; it does not run the Linux-only native
denial test or the physical runner. Graphify retained the existing
`host_abi.h` parser warning and skipped unsupported header/metadata files.

**Review:** independent Sol-medium code and documentation reviews completed
without remaining findings after two implementation fixes: exact prefix-stream
admission and wrapping effective-address calculation. The added callback-memory
and runner CLI regressions were re-reviewed clean. No Mac mini, SSH, hardware,
or physical results are claimed.

## S2-39e — exact Long64 FXRSTOR64 `[RBX+0x40]`

Added the strict local interpreter profile `s2-long-fxrstor64-rbx-disp8-v1`
for exactly `48 0F AE 4B 40`. The address is architectural wrapping
`RBX+0x40`; before access the full 512-byte image must be 16-byte aligned,
canonical48 and non-overflowing. x87/SSE snapshots are required, while
instruction/data selectors remain independently optional and are preserved as
provided.

The executor issues 13 ascending read-only callbacks for `[0,5)`, `[6,16)`,
`[16,24)`, `[24,28)`, eight 10-byte logical stack slots, and `[160,416)`. It
does not read reserved, padding, incoming MXCSR_MASK, or software tail bytes.
All fields are staged; loaded MXCSR is checked using the immutable target mask
`TARGET_FXSAVE_MXCSR_MASK` (`0x0000ffbf`) before any x87/SSE or RIP commit.
The image mask is ignored. A read or validation error leaves CPU state,
definedness, RIP and retirement unchanged and stops callbacks at the first
failure; backend categories are preserved and no external rollback is claimed.

The restore copies raw FCW/FSW, full FIP/FDP, low 11 FOP bits, raw 80-bit
payloads and XMM0–15. TOP maps logical image slots to physical registers;
abridged FTW marks empty physical slots, while nonempty values are classified
from exponent, full significand and J. Payload bits are unchanged, even for
empty slots and signaling NaNs. Selectors retain their original Option values.
The independent literal fixture has nonzero ignored/reserved bytes and a forged
MXCSR_MASK; tests cover all TOP values, selector combinations, FTW tag classes,
XMM payloads, forbidden MXCSR bits, callback failures, range preflight,
wrapping arithmetic and bounded FXSAVE64→mutate→FXRSTOR64 round-trip for
representable tag state. Abridged FTW does not preserve arbitrary nonempty tag
classes, so no arbitrary tag-word round-trip is claimed.

The strict decoder/profile regressions admit only this form. The CLI fixture
passed with the interpreter and returned Unsupported for JIT and native-x86.
**Verification:** `cargo test -p od-isa --lib --offline` passed (1,380/1,380);
`cargo test -p od-testkit fxrstor64 --offline` passed (1/1);
`cargo test -p od-runner --test fixture_v2 local_fxrstor64_rbx_fixture_runs_only_in_the_interpreter --offline`
passed (1/1); `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace
--all-targets --offline`, `cargo check -p od-x86-runner --all-targets --target
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --offline`, `git diff --check`, and `graphify update .`
passed. The Linux-target command was compile-only on this Apple ARM host.

Independent Sol-medium review identified two verification gaps, a stale plan
status, broken links and wording mismatches. The author corrected the expected
tag oracle, added architectural #PF, MXCSR bit-6 and incoming-mask invariance
coverage, updated the MAXPS/MINPD neighbor cases, and corrected the documentation.
Final independent Sol-medium code and documentation re-review completed with no
remaining findings. No SSH, Mac mini, physical x86, Linux
runtime, guest exception delivery, broader addressing forms, or general S2-39
acceptance is claimed. Those hardware checks stay in the combined final substage.

## S2-39f — bounded FXSAVE64 CR0 EM and TS `#NM` gates

Added the strict local profile `s2-long-fxsave64-cr0-gates-v1` for exactly

FXSR=1 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 remain fixed preconditions. Complete fetch/decode and
incoming STOP/zero-budget ordering are preserved. Either CR0 bit set reports
fault vector 7, no error code, zero retirement and no CPU/RAM commit or
data-memory callback at CPL0–3. With both clear, execution reuses the S2-39d
serializer. No SSE `#UD` helper is reused.

The independent hand-authored success image verifies all 512 bytes, including
preserved holes, pending x87 invalid/exception-summary state and MXCSR sticky
flags. The fault fixture compares complete CPU state and unchanged RAM. Strict
control shape, result echo/compare and S2-39d backward compatibility are
covered. Data-address/page fault versus gate priority, CR4.OSFXSR=0, FXSR=0,
alternate layouts, CPUID/CR writes, general CR support, FXRSTOR expansion,
JIT/native/C adapter and physical behavior are not established. Intel SDM
Rev. 093 Vol. 2A FXSAVE 64-Bit Mode Exceptions pp. 3-418–3-419 lists `#NM`
for CR0.TS and CR0.EM; Vol. 3A Event 7 pp. 7-33–7-34 states this is a fault,

## S2-40a — Ubuntu Generic amd64 requirement/evidence matrix

This documentation-only slice records the user's choice of Generic `amd64`
for Ubuntu 26.04.1 with an x86-64-v1 ABI/ISA floor. The requirement-to-owner
matrix, evidence limits, validation tiers, and single deferred Mac mini batch
are in the [Linux profile report](STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-40a--матрица-требований-ubuntu-generic-amd64).
It distinguishes static config/source/exact-image reachability from observed
runtime execution and explicitly avoids treating x86-64-v1 as the complete
kernel/userspace contract. No extension beyond v1 is proven necessary yet, but
the C/D inventory is incomplete, so this does not establish that all extensions
are globally unnecessary. No CPUID bits were added and no profile-complete
claim is made.

**Result and check criteria:** the matrix maps requirement groups to source and
image evidence, bounded local slices, missing semantics, an independent oracle
category, and an owning task/stage. CPU-only fixtures, Linux user-mode physical
oracle, privileged/system validation, and Stage 4 machine integration are
separated. All deferred Mac mini hardware checks appear once as `not_run` in the
Linux profile report and remain batched into one final hardware substage.
S2-41 is not ready for acceptance without a real machine backend. The bounded
SSE-only user-mode oracle contract is now documented separately in S2-40b; it
does not settle guest FXSAVE target mask/layout or selector differences, and
existing x87/SIMD fixtures are not thereby enabled for native comparison.

The documentation and its Markdown links are the only checks for this slice;

## S2-40b — bounded SSE-only native XORPD oracle

Implemented `s2-long-native-xorpd-xmm0-xmm1-v1` as an exact one-instruction
profile for `66 0F 57 C1` (`XORPD XMM0,XMM1`). The strict schema requires
XMM0–XMM15, MXCSR exactly `0x1f80`, ordinary integer input, no x87 state,
budget 1, stop RIP `entry+4`, and a single executable code mapping. The
interpreter reuses the existing raw-bit XOR semantics but permits the exact
XMM0/XMM1 form with SSE state and no x87 snapshot; existing general XORPD
forms retain their x87+SSE precondition. Literal expected XMM0 outputs are
handwritten independently in tests for two asymmetric fixtures. Tests also
check all other XMM sentinels, MXCSR, GPRs, flags, RIP, malformed code, missing
SSE, x87-present rejection and wrong MXCSR.

The runner adds a portable 16-register/MXCSR codec and exact readback check.
Linux x86_64 transport uses libc's `user_fpregs_struct`: `PTRACE_GETFPREGS`
reads the full FP-register structure, the runner replaces only XMM0–XMM15 and
MXCSR fields, and `PTRACE_SETFPREGS` writes the structure back. It verifies the
initial values before stepping and reads final SSE state separately from
integer registers. The supervisor, deadline and EXITKILL paths
are unchanged. This is Linux ptrace transport, not guest FXSAVE format; no host
MXCSR mask is substituted. Existing x87/SSE and FXSAVE profiles remain
native-denied. JIT and C adapter remain denied; CPUID target bits are unchanged.

**Checks:** `cargo test -p od-isa xorpd --offline` passed (3 tests);

`cargo test -p od-runner local_native_xorpd --offline` passed (1);
`cargo test -p od-x86-runner --bin od-x86-runner native_fp::tests --offline`
passed (3); `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, the Linux

x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and

documentation review found no remaining findings after the recorded fixes. Physical execution was not run; status
remains `not_run` for the final Mac mini substage. S2-26, S2-39, S2-40, S2-41
and S2-42 remain open. See [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-40b--bounded-sse-only-native-xorpd-oracle),

## S2-38b — точечные SSE2 prerequisite gates для XORPD

Добавлен отдельный schema-v2 profile `s2-long-xorpd-prerequisites-v1` для
строго `66 0F 57 C1` (`XORPD XMM0,XMM1`). Он требует явный блок неизменяемых
SSE2/CR0.EM/CR0.TS/CR4.OSFXSR inputs. Decoder завершает полный instruction
fetch до проверки: `!SSE2 || CR0.EM || !CR4.OSFXSR` даёт CPU-side #UD, затем
`CR0.TS` даёт #NM, иначе работает прежняя bytewise XORPD реализация.
Стандартная проверка CPL0–3 × 16 комбинаций даёт 14 #UD, 1 #NM и 1 success;
faults без error code не retire и сохраняют полный CPU snapshot. Данные
memory callbacks отсутствуют. Boundary tests покрывают fetch truncation,
STOP, zero budget, отсутствующее SSE snapshot и neighboring encoding.

`s2_38b_xorpd_sse2_absent.case.json` — рукописная literal fault fixture.
Схема отклоняет missing profile controls и посторонние формы. JIT остаётся
отклонён, а native runner относит профиль к local-only set. CPUID и C ABI не
менялись; OSXMMEXCPT/#XM не добавлены. Отдельные старые XORPD и S2-40b
profiles не перенастроены. Runner повторяет control inputs в result snapshot;
`v2::compare` сверяет обе oracle observations и input fixture, а старые result
snapshots сохраняют прежнюю JSON форму, поскольку поле пропускается для иных
profiles.

## S2-38c — exact MINSS unmasked invalid-operation exit

only `F3 0F 5D C1` (`MINSS XMM0,XMM1`). The profile requires explicit immutable
SSE availability, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT controls; full fetch
precedes gates. SSE unavailable, EM=1 or OSFXSR=0 raises CPU-side #UD before
TS=#NM. When a newly detected invalid condition is unmasked, IE is committed
to MXCSR before arithmetic #UD/#XM, while full XMM0, RIP and retirement remain
unchanged. Existing masked MINSS semantics are reused. The profile rejects
all forms except the one exact encoding, remains JIT/native/C-adapter denied,
and does not add generic CR writes or CPUID changes.

The fixture and result schema echo the explicit controls, compare them against
the bound fixture, and omit the new optional field for old profiles. The
handwritten literal fixture combines QNaN and subnormal with IM=0 and
