coverage includes all 32 gate/OSXMMEXCPT control combinations at CPL0–3, all
QNaN/SNaN source-class combinations across RC values, and both arithmetic
delivery vectors. No physical/Mac mini execution was run; its status remains
`not_run` until the combined final hardware substage. Broader S2-38, parent

## S2-38d — exact MINSS unmasked denormal-operand handling

Added `s2-long-minss-unmasked-denormal-v1` for only the existing exact Long64
`F3 0F 5D C1` (`MINSS XMM0,XMM1`) profile. The S2-38c
`s2-long-minss-invalid-controls-v1` contract remains unchanged. The new profile
reuses its five immutable controls and permits IM and DM independently while
requiring ZM/OM/UM/PM set, DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved MXCSR bits zero. Existing
entry gates still run before operand classification. With an effective
subnormal and DM=0, DE is committed before #UD/#XM, and XMM0, RIP and retirement
are suppressed; pre-existing DE alone does not fault. New fixtures cover
arithmetic #UD, #XM, an exception-free result and a mixed masked-invalid /
unmasked-denormal case. JIT, native and C-adapter admission remain unavailable.

For MINSS NaN plus subnormal, the tested mask matrix follows Rev. 093:
both-unmasked and mixed masked/unmasked pairs set IE|DE and deliver one fault;
both-masked sets only IE and completes the masked invalid result. In the mixed
and both-unmasked fault cases, OSXMMEXCPT selects vector 6 or 19. This reflects
Vol. 1 §11.5.3.2–3 flag commitment and §4.9.2 both-masked priority, with MINSS
exception classes from Vol. 2B. Tests cover QNaN and SNaN in both operand
orders for IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT, exact flags/vector/destination/RIP/retirement, and

## S2-38m — exact MINSS unmasked memory profile at m32 [RAX]

Added the interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-minss-memory-unmasked-rax-v1`
for exact Long64 `F3 0F 5D 00`. The pre-existing masked-only
`s2-long-minss-memory-rax-v1` profile remains unchanged. The profile has
immutable SSE, CR0.EM/TS and CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT controls, with CR0.MP=1 fixed.
Full fetch precedes #UD/#NM gates; supported MXCSR/state checks precede AC=1
local Unsupported; checked canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+3]` precedes exactly one
read4. AC=0 permits unaligned access. Address/read failures suppress FP
classification and leave state/retirement unchanged.

The profile uses S2-38d's mixed IM/DM MINSS policy: IM/DM vary independently,
ZM/OM/UM/PM remain set, DAZ/FTZ/reserved bits are clear, and all RC and sticky
histories are admitted. Unmasked IE/DE commits sticky status, suppresses the
whole XMM0 write and retirement, and exits via #XM or arithmetic #UD according
to OSXMMEXCPT. The independent raw-bit schema oracle validates RHS selection
and result state; the literal QNaN fixture covers #XM. Direct ISA tests cover
the IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT matrix, RC×64 histories, source classes/order, controls,
combined faults, callback counts, atomicity and poisoned XMM state. Native,
JIT, C ABI, generic and fragment paths remain closed.

Focused checks passed: `od-isa` S2-38m tests (2) and runner fixture test (1).
After integrating S2-30dm and S2-38m into main, combined suites passed:
`od-isa` 1,891; `od-testkit` 455; runner 125 unit + 518 fixtures;
`od-x86-runner` 8 library + 4 binary. Workspace all-target offline check,
formatting, diff, layout and Graphify update passed. Separate Sol/high review is
clean after exact-form, backend-relabel and documentation fixes; details are in
the standalone [S2-38m report](S2_38M_MINSS_MEMORY_UNMASKED.md). No
physical x86 or complete SSE/MMX acceptance is claimed. ISSUE-025 stays open
and concerns the unrelated RCPSS/RCPPS threshold. See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38m-exact-long64-minss-xmm0m32-rax-memory-profile-with-mixed-imdm-exit),
[CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-38m--exact-minss-unmasked-memory-exit-for-m32-rax),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-38m--minss-xmm0m32-rax-with-unmasked-imdm).

## S2-38n — exact MAXSS unmasked memory profile at m32 [RAX]

Added interpreter-only schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-maxss-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact Long64 `F3 0F 5F 00`
(`MAXSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]`). The S2-37cy masked memory profile and S2-38f
register profile remain separate and unchanged. The new immutable controls
echo SSE, CR0.EM/TS/MP and CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT; CR0.MP must be one. Fetch and
exact-form selection precede SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM gates; MXCSR/state
checks precede AC=1 local refusal; checked canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+3]` precedes
one read4. AC=0 permits unaligned m32, and address/read faults precede FP
classification.

MAXSS-specific behavior is retained from S2-38f: either QNaN or SNaN raises
IE, either subnormal raises DE, and masked MAXSS selects raw source 2 on NaN,
equal values and signed-zero ties, including an unquieted source-2 SNaN payload.
With NaN+subnormal and both masks set, invalid priority reports IE only; if
either mask is open, IE|DE are committed on one arithmetic exit. A new
unmasked event suppresses all of XMM0 and retirement while updating MXCSR
stickies; OSXMMEXCPT selects #XM or arithmetic #UD. The independent schema
oracle checks raw MAXSS output and complete result state. Tests cross
IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT, RC×64 sticky histories and operand classes/orders, and cover
exact-form-before-disabled-gates, AC/span/read fault priority, callback counts,
rollback, strict result/control echo, and JIT/native denial. The literal QNaN
fixture exercises #XM, with a masked companion completion in the runner test.

Integrated main verification passed: combined `od-isa` (1,895), `od-testkit`
(455), and `od-runner` (125 unit + 520 fixture) suites; `od-x86-runner` (8
library + 4 binary tests), workspace all-target offline check, formatting,
layout check, diff check, and Graphify refresh (11,828 nodes, 25,656 edges,
376 communities). Independent Sol/high review is clean. No physical x86
acceptance is claimed; ISSUE-025 remains unrelated to this profile. See the

`generate_fixture` и команда `--generate-corpus` не изменялись. Corpus,

завершают проверку ненулевым кодом. Handwritten checks независимо покрывают

## S2-42b — bounded native XORPD XMM-input reducer

Added a one-fixture reducer restricted to the existing
`s2-long-native-xorpd-xmm0-xmm1-v1` profile. `od-testkit` proposes changes only
to initial XMM0–XMM15, in a fixed single pass over whole registers, 8/4/2/1-byte
blocks, then set bits ordered byte0..15 and bit7..0. It skips no-ops and accepts
only lower total XMM Hamming weight plus two equal semantic callback results
whose XMM mismatch-position fingerprint matches the initial fingerprint.
Fingerprints use the independent bytewise-XOR oracle and exact mismatching
register/byte positions; incorrect byte values do not define the class. All
other state, retirement, successful stop, exception absence and code mapping
must match the oracle. The reducer makes no global-minimum claim.

`od-runner --reduce-native-xorpd CASE.json [--limit N] [--output-dir DIR]`
loads one strict fixture and uses the local interpreter callback. Every
candidate is serialized/revalidated and its oracle is recomputed from its own
XMM0/XMM1 input. The 5120 maximum actual-run budget includes two initial and two
reserved final confirmations; every candidate costs two calls. Output is
exclusive under ignored `work/stage2/s2-42b-xorpd/` and records fixture/result
hashes, initial/final interpreter results, expected oracle result(s),
fingerprints, counters, Hamming weights, provenance, revision/toolchain, replay
commands and `native=not_run`. A correct initial interpreter result is reported
as `no_initial_mismatch`, with no reduced fixture. Callback failures stop with
an incomplete report. Synthetic test callbacks are algorithm-only and are not
CPU/hardware evidence. The existing generated corpus was not modified.

**Checks:** `cargo test -p od-testkit --offline native_xorpd -- --nocapture`
(10 passed) covers deterministic reduction, XMM2–XMM15 dependencies, fingerprint
position/value behavior, no-op/refusal, budget 4/5/6, initial/candidate/final
flakiness, callback errors (including malformed short and odd-length XMM hex)
and no initial mismatch. The runner-specific
`cargo test -p od-runner --bin od-runner --offline native_xorpd_corpus_tests`
(5 passed) includes output integrity, raw-input digest binding for canonical,
whitespace and reordered-key fixtures, sidecar SHA-256 values and no-mismatch
reporting. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `git diff --check` and
`graphify update .` passed. `python3 tools/check_layout.py` reports the linked
worktree `.git` pointer and two unavailable old work-manifest links; these are
the existing layout/report conditions, not introduced by S2-42b. No physical
CPU, Mac mini or hardware callback ran (`native=not_run`).

The general S2-42 acceptance remains open, including instruction deletion,
branch target preservation, memory/REP and FP-fault groups, and physical
comparison. See [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-42b-bounded-xmm-input-reducer),
[format/replay](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-42b-bounded-native-xorpd-xmm-input-reducer),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-42b-native-xorpd-xmm-input-reducer).

## S2-27g — exact Long64 SWAPGS

Implemented exact bare `0F 01 F8` execution under explicit `SwapgsV1` with
observable exchange of `gs_base` and optional `kernel_gs_base`. The schema
profile is `s2-long-swapgs-v1`; legacy state defaults to `None`, and schema
serialization retains `Some(0)` while omitting the field for old profiles.
Fixture admission is limited to a single SWAPGS (budget 1), a double SWAPGS
(budget 2), and SWAPGS followed by exact GS qword load (budget 2). Distinct
literal qwords at old/new bases prove which address the load used; a separate
injected second-instruction page fault checks prior SWAPGS commit.
CPL1–3 #GP(0), missing profile/state, base canonicality, exact LOCK #UD fetch
ordering, neighbors, preservation, double/zero/equal bases, and budget/STOP
boundaries are covered by focused tests. The runner opts into this profile;
JIT, native, and C/fragment execution deny the new state/operation.

Author verification: `cargo test --workspace swapgs --offline -- --nocapture`,
`cargo test -p od-testkit swapgs --offline -- --nocapture`,

Independent Sol review found and then cleared a profile-export validation issue:
legacy profiles now reject present kernel-GS state, while SWAPGS export requires
canonical kernel-GS state. Linux/native execution and physical acceptance were
not performed. Architecture boundary: Intel SDM Rev. 093
Vol. 2B SWAPGS pp. 4-697–4-698, including its CR4.FRED restriction; FRED is

## S2-26g — bounded `KernelGsBaseV1` MSR and SWAPGS composition

Added independent `MsrProfile::KernelGsBaseV1` for `IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE`
(`0xC0000102`), limited to bare Long64 RDMSR/WRMSR. CPL0 reads return
zero-extended EDX:EAX; writes use low EDX:EAX, require canonical48, and mutate
only explicit `kernel_gs_base`. Missing state remains Unsupported. CPL1–3 and
noncanonical writes #GP(0) without commit or retirement. The existing
`run_with_msr_profile` does not enable SWAPGS; only the new combined interpreter
entry point selects both policies.

The v2 fixture profile requires canonical48 GS and kernel-GS state and admits
only the four requested exact programs and budgets. Literal cases demonstrate
RDMSR zero-extension, dirty upper WRMSR source halves, WRMSR→SWAPGS→RDMSR
reading the former active GS base, and WRMSR→SWAPGS→GS-load reading the distinct
qword at `0x2000`. The late injected load fault preserves both earlier commits,
reports two retirements and RIP at entry+5. Legacy SWAPGS fixture bytes and
digests were not changed. JIT and native runner profiles deny the new profile;
existing C/fragment adapters reject present kernel-GS state, including zero.

## S2-27h — exact Long64 `CLI`

Added `CliProfile::NonPviLong64V1` and the independent schema profile
`s2-long-cli-v1`. It admits bare `FA` under fixed Long64, CR0.PE=1, VM=0,
CR4.PVI=0, no VMX/SMM assumptions. CPL comes from the access context and IOPL
from RFLAGS[13:12]. CPL<=IOPL clears only IF, advances RIP one byte and
retires once even when IF was already clear. CPL>IOPL reports #GP(0) with no
state change, retirement or data callback regardless of IF. The arithmetic
`rflags_defined` mask remains unchanged; only this fixture profile admits and
compares concrete IF/IOPL alongside `INTEGER_FLAGS`.

The 32 handwritten fixture cases cover IF=0/1 × CPL0–3 × IOPL0–3 and produce
20 successful executions plus 12 #GP(0) results. Focused tests cover bare
profile admission, legacy denial, exact `F0 FA` #UD and fetch priority, other
prefix/neighbor denial, STOP and budget-before-fetch, plus a fresh-boundary
composition where a caller resubmits a new maskable request after CLI. The
IF=0 continuation executes NOP to RIP+2 without eligibility notification;
the IF=1 control reports `InterruptEligible` before fetch. Comparison tests
show either IF or IOPL tampering is detected. CPUID profile code and masks are
unchanged. JIT, native x86 and C/fragment APIs deny this profile.

Checks on 2026-10-29: focused CLI tests passed for the 32-case interpreter
matrix (20 successes/12 faults), fetch/STOP/budget/prefix boundaries, the
post-CLI interrupt-request composition, typed CPL/schema isolation, IF/IOPL
tampering, native local-only preflight, JIT and C denial. `cargo test -p od-testkit -p od-runner -p od-host
--offline` passed after the final edits (404 testkit, 112 runner unit, 361
runner fixture integration, 9 host tests; 0 failures). `cargo check --workspace
--all-targets --offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, Linux-target
`cargo check -p od-x86-runner --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --all-targets
--offline`, `git diff --check`, and `graphify update .` passed. The Linux-gated
native local-only helper test passed, and the Linux-gated native integration
preflight test compiles but could not run on this macOS host; a
Linux-target test-binary link attempt failed because Darwin `ld` does not accept

checks were not run; this local CPU profile does not model #GP/#UD delivery or
Linux execution. Independent Sol-medium review found the missing native

Table 3-7. See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-27h--exact-long64-cli), [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-27h--exact-long64-cli), [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-27h-exact-long64-cli-fixture-profile), and [Linux matrix](STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-27h-local-cli-matrix-entry).

## S2-27i — exact Long64 `STI` and one-instruction shadow

Added `StiProfile::NonPviLong64V1`, bare `FB` decoding, and explicit optional
`LongModeState::sti_shadow`. The profile requires a modeled shadow state,
applies the bounded Long64/non-PVI assumptions and the CPL/IOPL rule, sets IF,
and creates a one-instruction block only when IF was clear. The shared private
execution loop consumes that block only after a successful retirement. CLI
clears IF and shadow, and another STI with IF already set creates no new block.
Legacy paths reject active shadow state; maskable-request and interrupt
delivery reject it before eligibility/fetch or descriptor/stack callbacks.
Legacy REP continuation rejects it before token checks, stop callbacks, fetch,
data access or retirement. Native preflight treats the profile as local-only
before trace setup.

The `s2-long-sti-v1` fixture schema carries and compares shadow state and uses
`INTEGER_FLAGS|IF|IOPL` without changing arithmetic flag definedness. Its
literal privilege cases are supplemented by focused tests for resume,
double-STI, CLI, STOP/budget/fetch/unsupported preservation, active-shadow
request/REP rejection and compound-schema terminal-boundary validation. JIT,
native and C/fragment execution remain denied.

Architecture source: Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2B, STI pp. 4-674–4-675,
Table 4-22. NMI/SMI delivery details, HLT, MOV SS, scheduler effects and REP
boundary behavior are outside this slice. See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-27i--exact-long64-sti-and-maskable-interrupt-inhibition), [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-27i--exact-long64-sti-and-one-instruction-maskable-interrupt-shadow), [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-27i-exact-long64-sti-fixture-profile), and [Linux matrix](STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-27i-local-sti-matrix-entry).

**Checks:** five focused `od-isa` STI tests, the 16-case privilege/IF fixture
matrix, malformed compound fixture validation, active-shadow REP continuation
rejection, and native local-only helper tests passed. Workspace all-target
check, Linux x86-64 all-target compile check, formatting, diff check and
`graphify update .` passed. The Linux-only native execute preflight regression
compiled but was not run on macOS. Layout validation reports the linked-worktree
`.git` pointer and two pre-existing missing oracle manifests under `work/`.
Independent Sol-medium review found three issues—native preflight, REP
continuation bypass, and compound fixture terminal-boundary validation. All
were fixed and re-reviewed clean. No Linux runtime, SSH, physical or Mac mini
checks were run.

## S2-27j — exact Long64 HLT and synchronous maskable wake

Added `HaltProfile::Long64V1`, explicit optional `LongModeState::activity`,
and `RunExit::Halted`. Bare `F4` is admitted only under the bounded Long64
profile. CPL0 HLT retires once, advances RIP, preserves other modeled state,
consumes an active STI Blocking shadow and returns Halted immediately. CPL1–3
fault with #GP(0) atomically. Exact `F0 F4` fetches both bytes before #UD;
other prefixes stay unsupported.

Every public run, step and REP continuation boundary respects persistent
Halted state without fetching or retiring. IF=1 plus Clear shadow allows an
eligible caller-owned maskable request to be reported without waking or
consuming it; IF=0 stays Halted without fetch. Successful existing bounded
interrupt delivery transitions to Running after the complete frame stores
and saves the post-HLT RIP. Legacy `None` activity remains accepted, while
schema snapshots distinguish Running and Halted and fragment/native/C paths
deny the profile.

The `s2-long-hlt-v1` literal matrix covers 16 CPL/IF/IOPL combinations (four
Halted and twelve #GP(0)), plus `FB F4`, `FA F4`, and `FA FB F4`. Focused
coverage includes STI shadow consumption, atomic faults, fetch boundaries,
halted re-entry through run/step/REP, request eligibility, and interrupt frame
commit/wake composition.

## S2-25d — main-kernel IA32 EFER evidence and read-only candidate

Mapped `RDMSR IA32_EFER` (`0F 32`, index `0xc0000080`) at
`ffffffff8139c1b4` and conditional `WRMSR` at `ffffffff8139c1d5` to the
authenticated Ubuntu `common_startup_64` source/image. The code always sets
SCE and conditionally sets NXE/`early_pmd_flags.NX` when
CPUID.80000001:EDX[20] reports NX; it skips WRMSR if the low EFER value is
unchanged. The selected synthetic target advertises NX. This is a mapped
main-kernel direct64 continuation, not a claim that no earlier compressed or
helper path accesses EFER, and not runtime observation. The 32-bit compressed
entry's EFER access is bypassed by the selected direct64 prefix; transitive
`__pi_*` and decompression-helper ordering remains unaudited.

No runtime EFER field or general MSR map was added. The bounded read-only
profile is implemented separately as S2-25e over synthetic values `0x500`,
`0x501`, `0xd00`, `0xd01`; these are not asserted to be Ubuntu's entry value.
WRMSR, LMA transitions, NX enforcement and paging/TLB effects remain outside
CPU-only scope. The adjacent compiled CR0 load is `0x80050033`
(including AM), unlike S2-25a's synthetic `0x80010033`; actual entry CR0 is
unobserved. See the [source/image evidence](STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#ia32-efer-on-the-mapped-main-kernel-direct64-continuation),
[contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-25d--ia32-efer-evidence-and-read-only-candidate),

and [open evidence limitation](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md#issue-027--first-efer-access-and-startup-control-snapshot-are-unproven).

## S2-38h — exact Long64 MAXSD with bounded unmasked IM/DM exits

**Status:** local interpreter/schema-v2 implementation, focused validation, and independent `gpt-6.1-sol` review complete with no findings. Physical/Mac mini acceptance remains `not_run` and is deferred to the final hardware substage.

Added the distinct `s2-long-maxsd-unmasked-denormal-v1` profile for exact
`F2 0F 5F C1`. Immutable MAXSD controls hold SSE2, CR0.EM/TS and
CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT; complete fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD, then TS #NM,

reserved bits, DAZ and FTZ must be clear; ZE/OE/UE/PE masks are set; IM, DM, RC
and prior sticky bits are allowed. The old masked MAXSD/MINSD execution path is

both masks set completes with IE only; if IM or DM is open, IE|DE are committed

and RIP and retire zero; completion changes only XMM0 low qword. No handler
continuation, native, JIT, C or fragment admission is claimed.

The 88 fixed literal fixture inputs comprise the NaN/SNaN/subnormal/mixed class

snapshots using raw classification and an independent ordering rule; runner
coverage includes output/control tampering, comparator rejection, and JIT/native
denial. Verification passed: two named `od-isa` S2-38h matrix tests and one
runner integration test over all 88 fixtures. The ISA matrix also checks

## S2-37m — exact Long64 CVTDQ2PD XMM0,XMM1

Implemented decoder and interpreter support only through schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtdq2pd-reg-exact-v1` for exact bytes `F3 0F E6 C1`. The selected
profile requires one executable mapping, budget one, stop RIP `entry+4`, and
explicit echoed SSE2, CR0.EM/TS and CR4.OSFXSR controls. Complete-fetch gate
ordering is #UD for absent SSE2/EM/OSFXSR, then #NM for TS, at CPL0–3. Faults
preserve full CPU state and retire zero instructions.

Success converts signed dwords XMM1[31:0] and XMM1[63:32] exactly to binary64
and replaces all of XMM0. XMM1 high64 and all unrelated state are preserved;
MXCSR is unchanged for supported bits `0x0000ffbf`. The independent schema
validator constructs IEEE binary64 encodings from integer sign/magnitude and
leading-bit position; it does not use the production `Binary64::from_i64`
helper. Six handwritten fixtures cover zero, ±1, i32 endpoints, asymmetric
lanes, values around 2^24 and NaN-like integer bit patterns. JIT/native fixture
execution is explicitly refused.

The profile refuses memory, REX/register-extension, repeated/reordered prefix,
non-C1 ModR/M, VEX and EVEX forms without making architectural #UD claims for
each exclusion. It does not enable generic CPUID SSE2 admission, implement
other CVTDQ2PD forms, memory faults, JIT, C/fragment paths, or close S2-37.
Physical validation remains reserved for the combined final Mac mini
substage. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTDQ2PD pp. 3-208–3-210; §2.5
Table 2-15 p. 2-24 and §2.5.5 Table 2-22 p. 2-30
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37m--exact-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm0xmm1),
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37m--exact-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm0xmm1),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37m-local-cvtdq2pd).

supported sticky/mask/RC/FTZ combinations, unsupported DAZ/reserved MXCSR,
malformed/truncated forms, zero budget, state preservation and no data

mapping, budget one and stop RIP `entry+5`. It reads full RAX as signed i64,
converts with `Binary64::from_i64` under MXCSR.RC, changes only XMM0 low64 on
completion, and preserves XMM0 high64, RAX and unrelated state. S2-37n r32
remains distinct. Other REX values, r32, other indices, memory, other or
reordered/repeated prefixes, other opcodes, VEX and EVEX remain profile
refusals.

The existing local MXCSR mask `0x0000ffbf` applies; DAZ=1 and reserved bits
reject, and FTZ does not affect integer conversion. Only Precision can be new.
Sticky PE is committed before an unmasked inexact exception. PM=0 suppresses
destination update and retirement, then raises #XM with OSXMMEXCPT=1 or
SIMD-generated #UD with it clear. PM=1 commits the rounded result and PE.
Exact conversions do not fault from old PE. Full fetch precedes prerequisite
#UD (SSE2/EM/OSFXSR) and #NM (TS); prerequisite faults do not mutate state.
`i64::MAX → 2^63` under applicable rounding is a valid finite result.

Sixteen literal fixtures cover signed endpoints, exact values, ties, directed
rounding, the power-boundary carry, masked completion and both precision fault
paths. The independent schema oracle uses signed magnitude plus explicit
53-bit remainder and RC rounding, without production conversion helpers or
host FP. ISA tests exercise the full RC × PM × OSXMMEXCPT × old-PE matrix,
prerequisite CPL0–3, malformed/truncated forms, STOP/budget and state/access
preservation. Runner tests validate fixtures and controls, PE-before-fault,
result tampering, and JIT/native denial.

`cargo test -p od-testkit cvtsi2sd_r64_independent_oracle --offline`, and

fragment adapter continues rejecting states with SSE payloads.

requires one executable mapping, budget one and checked stop RIP, and rejects

ORed into sticky PE only; the other MXCSR bits remain intact. For unmasked

rounding, i32 endpoints and zero, malformed encodings, tampering, and JIT/native
denial. The lane-3-only case verifies atomic whole-destination suppression.

## S2-37ab — canonical Long64 CVTSS2SI register space

Implemented interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtss2si-registers-v1`
for 512 canonical register forms. The decoder uses F3 0F 2D /r for r32 and F3
REX.W 0F 2D /r for r64, with ModR/M.mod=3 and canonical REX.R/B extension.
Execution reads XMM low32, applies MXCSR.RC via `Binary32::to_i32/to_i64`,
zero-extends r32 results, and preserves all other GPR/XMM/RFLAGS state. IE and PE
are distinct new events: invalid yields integer indefinite and suppresses PE;
valid inexact conversion raises PE. Sticky status commits before unmasked #XM or
SIMD #UD, while destination/RIP/retirement remain suppressed. Subnormal input
with DM unmasked produces no DE. Fetch/gates occur before conversion and no data
memory is accessed. DAZ/reserved MXCSR settings, unsupported encodings and
JIT/native/generic/C/fragment execution remain refused.

The testkit has a separate integer-only raw-bit parser and rounding oracle.
Runner coverage constructs all 512 selector pairs with distinct XMM low32
values, checks r32 zero-extension and source selection, and executes both-width
rounding, signed boundaries around ±2^31 and ±2^63, invalid/precision priority,
exact minimum versus indefinite, sticky status, masked and unmasked faults, and
the subnormal/DM boundary. OSXMMEXCPT=0 produces SIMD #UD for an unmasked event.
The interpreter checks complete fetch and gate priority at CPL0–3, plus STOP,
zero budget, truncated fetch, DAZ/reserved MXCSR refusal, and cross-profile
denial. JIT/native denial and tampered control/fault metadata are covered. No
physical oracle or Mac mini execution was performed. Memory
forms and broader CPU acceptance remain open. Parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open.

## S2-37af — canonical Long64 CVTPS2DQ XMM register pairs

The schema-v2 interpreter profile `s2-long-cvtps2dq-registers-v1` accepts all
256 XMM destination/source pairs in Long64. It requires `66 0F 5B /r`,
ModR/M.mod=3, and exactly one REX `41`, `44`, or `45` after `66` when an XMM
index is extended. Memory, REX.W/X/40, repeated/reordered/other prefixes,
trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are bounded-profile refusals only. Runtime
admission is independent of CVTDQ2PS; JIT, native, C ABI, fragment and generic
CPUID paths remain closed.

Execution snapshots the complete source before writing, rounds all four raw
binary32 lanes using MXCSR.RC, then checks signed-i32 range. A masked invalid
lane returns `0x80000000`; exact −2^31 remains valid. New IE is accumulated
before computation; new PE is accumulated only from valid inexact lanes. With
IM=0, any new IE commits IE and faults before adding PE from another lane. With
IM=1, invalid lanes do not suppress PE from valid inexact lanes; IE|PE is
committed and PM controls the post-computation fault. Old sticky bits are
preserved and alone do not fault. Unmasked new IE/PE suppresses the entire XMM
destination, RIP and retirement, then selects #XM or SIMD-generated #UD by
OSXMMEXCPT. This conversion raises no DE; the local profile rejects DAZ and
ignores FTZ.

Full fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM gates at CPL0–3. No data
memory callbacks occur. The result oracle classifies and rounds raw `u32` bits
with independent integer arithmetic. It exercises the complete lane-event ×
RC × masks × OSXMMEXCPT × sticky-status matrix, aliases, tie and signed-range
boundaries, subnormals, atomic destination suppression, gates/fetch and strict
metadata refusal. Memory m128, other modes, hardware acceptance, and parent
S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Hardware evidence is reserved for the combined final
stage.

Focused verification passed:

- `cargo test -p od-runner cvtps2dq_register_pairs_and_ie_pe_ordering_matrix --offline` — directly runs the unmasked literal lane-0 IE/lane-3 PE fixture and verifies IE-only status, atomic XMM/RIP and zero retirement; also covers all 256 register pairs plus 10,368 lane-event/RC/IM/PM/OSXMMEXCPT/old-IE-PE cases, a separate masked-IE/PM-unmasked IE|PE case, rounding and signed-range vectors, DM-clear subnormals, malformed bytes, metadata tampering, profile cross-denial and JIT/native denial.

### S2-37aj — SQRTSS register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-sqrtss-registers-v1` for all 256 canonical Long64 `F3 [REX] 0F 51 /r` XMM register pairs. Strict encoding accepts four-byte low-register forms and five-byte extended forms requiring REX `41`, `44`, or `45` directly after F3; memory, REX.W/X/40, other/reordered/duplicate prefixes, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are rejected. Generic, JIT, native, C ABI and fragment execution remain closed.

The source low32 is snapshotted before commit; MXCSR.RC selects rounding and only destination low32 changes. High96 and unrelated architectural state are retained. DAZ/reserved MXCSR encodings are refused; all RCs, FTZ, masks and prior sticky bits are accepted. The local raw helper preserves signed zero, preserves QNaN bits, quiets SNaN by setting the quiet bit with IE, and returns IE plus `0xffc00000` for negative nonzero values. This is the helper's value policy and is not a hardware NaN payload guarantee. Positive subnormal reports precompute DE; if masked, calculation continues and can set PE. Negative subnormal follows the other-invalid path and reports IE only; that terminal SQRTSS path does not also report DE even when IM is masked. Unmasked DE stops before calculation and PE. Unmasked SIMD outcomes commit newly raised status before #XM when OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise, while destination/RIP/retirement remain atomic. Full fetch precedes SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM; there are no data callbacks. FTZ is irrelevant because finite positive square-root results are normal.

Local verification passed:

- `cargo test -p od-isa sqrtss_register_decodes_all_xmm_pairs_and_rejects_other_encodings --offline` — 2 tests passed, including all 256 canonical pair decodes and malformed-neighbor rejection; the paired RSQRTSS decoder test also passed.
- `cargo test -p od-isa sqrtss_fetch_and_sse_gates_are_cpl_independent --offline` — passed truncated-fetch priority and SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD / TS #NM atomicity with CS RPL 0–3.
- `cargo test -p od-testkit sqrtss_parser_and_oracle_cover_register_space_and_special_values --offline` — passed the all-pair schema parser and independent integer-square-root raw-u32 oracle, including all four RC modes, signed zero, NaNs, infinities, negative inputs and signed subnormals.
- `cargo test -p od-runner sqrtss_literal_fixture_executes_only_in_interpreter_profile --offline` — passed the literal exact-square fixture and JIT/native denial.
- `cargo test -p od-runner sqrtss_all_pairs_events_controls_and_sticky_status --offline` — passed all 256 destination/source pairs, 8 input classes × IM/DM/PM × OSXMMEXCPT, live execution with all four RC values and FTZ set, four SSE/CR gates and 8 prior-sticky combinations. Result validation checks exception vector, status, full-state atomicity, RIP and retirement.

Общие проверки прошли: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `python3 tools/check_layout.py`, `git diff --check`, `graphify update .`. Независимый review ожидает передачи; его результат будет добавлен после review. Физическое исполнение x86 не запускалось, physical acceptance остаётся в combined final stage. Memory forms, other execution modes, DAZ и reserved MXCSR values находятся вне этого локального профиля. ### S2-37ak — SQRTPS register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-sqrtps-registers-v1` for all 256 canonical Long64 `0F 51 /r` register pairs. Low forms are three bytes; extended indices require exactly one REX `41`, `44`, or `45` before `0F` for length four. Mandatory/other/redundant/reordered prefixes, REX.W/X/40, memory forms, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are refused. Generic, JIT, native, C ABI and fragment execution remain closed. SQRTPS gates on SSE (not SSE2), CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR, then CR0.TS.

Execution snapshots all four source lanes and replaces all 128 destination bits only on successful completion. The profile rejects DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits; it accepts all RC modes, FTZ, masks and old sticky bits. Per lane, negative nonzero finite/infinity and SNaN raise precompute IE; negative subnormal is terminal IE-only for that lane. QNaN, including negative QNaN, does not raise IE. SNaN quieting and NaN sign/payload bits follow the local `Binary32::sqrt_raw_result` policy and are not asserted as hardware payload guarantees. A positive subnormal contributes precompute DE. IE and DE aggregate across all lanes before computation: if any new pre-event is unmasked, all generated IE/DE bits are committed and no new PE is computed or recorded. If pre-events are masked, all four results are computed with MXCSR.RC and PE aggregates afterward. Unmasked status commits before #XM when OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise; every unmasked event suppresses the full XMM destination, RIP and retirement. FTZ does not alter finite positive square-root outputs.

The schema-v2 oracle independently classifies raw `u32` lanes and uses integer square-root rounding, with packed event aggregation independent of the interpreter. Focused local verification passed:

- `cargo test -p od-isa sqrtps_ --offline` — 6 passed, including all 256 decoder pairs, malformed neighbors, direct public runtime MXCSR admission, SSE/EM/OSFXSR/TS gates, fetch-before-gate, no data callbacks, pre-event aggregation and atomicity.
- `cargo test -p od-isa sqrtss --offline` — 5 passed; neighboring SQRTSS controls and existing runtime profile still pass after the invalid/NaN classifier update.
- `cargo test -p od-testkit sqrtps_parser_and_packed_raw_oracle_aggregate_lane_events --offline` — passed parser coverage for 256 register pairs and raw-u32 lane value/event/RC checks.
- `cargo test -p od-runner sqrtps_literal_fixture_executes_only_in_interpreter_profile --offline` — passed the literal fixture, result/control tamper checks, DAZ/reserved rejection and JIT/native denial.
- `cargo test -p od-runner sqrtps_all_pairs_lane_events_and_control_matrix --offline` — passed all destination/source pairs, per-lane placement of IE/DE/PE and special classes, all 24 cross-lane IE|DE|PE permutations × IM/DM/PM/OSXMMEXCPT, RC/FTZ, old sticky flags, full-state result/exception validation and backend denial.

The full workspace/layout checks and independent review remain pending. No physical x86 execution was performed, and this local evidence is not physical acceptance. Memory forms and other execution modes remain outside the profile; parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B SQRTPS pp. 4-664–4-666 ([Vol. 2B](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)); Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.1–.2 and 11.5.3.1–.3 ([Vol. 1](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); Vol. 3A Event 19 and Table 7-8 ([Vol. 3A](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)); Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13 ([PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/786447/floating-point-reference-sheet-for-intel-architecture.pdf)).

### S2-37ap — SUBSD register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented the strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile
`s2-long-subsd-registers-v1` for all 256 canonical Long64 `F2 0F 5C /r` XMM
register pairs. It rejects memory, alternate/redundant/reordered prefixes,
REX.W/X/40, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX. Full fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR
#UD and TS #NM gates at CPL0–3. The profile makes no data callbacks and remains
closed to JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic execution.

The bounded masked-range contract requires MXCSR.OM=1 and MXCSR.UM=1; it rejects
DAZ/reserved bits and accepts all RC, FTZ, IM/DM/PM and sticky settings. Both XMMs
are snapshotted; only old destination.low64 minus source.low64 is computed,
destination.high64 is preserved bit-for-bit, and source.high64 is ignored. NaNs
are selected before RHS sign inversion, with destination NaN priority, SNaN
quieting/IE, QNaN without IE alone, and NaN suppression of DE. Same-sign
infinities produce IE/indefinite; otherwise low64 subnormals produce DE. New
IE/DE precede arithmetic. Masked overflow contributes OE|PE, inexact tiny
results UE|PE, and FTZ flushes tiny results to signed zero. Unmasked events commit
sticky status but preserve full XMM/RIP/retirement.

Local evidence: the literal fixture and runner test pass; the runner checks all
256 register pairs and aliases, source-high poison and destination-high
preservation, QNaN/SNaN, infinity-invalid, denormal, FTZ, masked overflow,
unmasked PM/DM atomicity, result tampering and JIT/native denial. The raw-u64
integer schema oracle is independent of the production arithmetic helper. The
production runtime test passes all four RC halfway cases, PM atomicity, SSE2/EM/
OSFXSR/TS gates at CPL0–3 and no data callbacks. The decoder test passes all 256
pairs and malformed prefix/memory/VEX/EVEX refusals. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`,
`git diff --check` and `graphify update .` passed. Independent review was clean with the fixture provenance, DE-before-PE/IM=0 coverage and CPL context corrections applied.
This is local evidence, not physical acceptance;
memory operands, other modes, full unmasked OE/UE and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain
open. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A Type 3, Table 2-20; Vol. 2B SUBSD
instruction entry; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.3; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8.
See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37ap--bounded-masked-range-long64-subsd-xmm-register-pairs),
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37ap--bounded-masked-range-long64-subsd-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37ap-bounded-masked-range-subsd-register-pair).
### S2-37aq — SUBSS register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented strict schema-v2 profile `s2-long-subss-registers-v1` for all 256
canonical Long64 `F3 0F 5C /r` register pairs. It rejects memory and noncanonical
prefix forms, and full fetch precedes SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM gates. The
operation performs no data callbacks and remains denied to JIT/native/C ABI,
fragment and generic execution.

Schema and runtime require OM=UM=1, reject DAZ/reserved MXCSR bits and accept
all RC, FTZ, IM/DM/PM and old sticky settings. Both XMM operands are snapshotted;
only low32 is subtracted, destination high96 is preserved, and source high96 is
ignored. The first original NaN is selected before RHS sign inversion; SNaN
raises IE, QNaN alone does not, and NaNs suppress DE. Same-sign infinity
subtraction returns `0xffc00000` with IE. Other subnormal operands raise DE.
Masked overflow records OE|PE; inexact tiny and FTZ-flushed results record
UE|PE. Unmasked new events commit status without changing XMM/RIP/retirement.
The schema oracle is an independent raw-u32 integer implementation with no host
FP or production arithmetic helper.

The literal fixture and focused 256-pair runner matrix pass, including all-RC
execution, NaN ordering and quieting (lhs QNaN/rhs SNaN, lhs SNaN/rhs QNaN,
both SNaN, and rhs-only SNaN), infinity/DE/FTZ/overflow cases, runtime gates
and unmasked-precision atomicity. The testkit raw-u32 oracle, production
runtime unit test, SUBSD and SUBPS runner regressions also pass. Review found
and corrected RHS-selected SNaN quieting; no code findings remain. The fixture
provenance table reference was aligned to Type 3/Table 2-20. `cargo fmt --all
-- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`,
`git diff --check` and `graphify update .` pass. The repository layout did not
change, so the layout checker was not applicable. This is local evidence, not
physical acceptance; memory forms, other modes and full unmasked OE/UE behavior
remain outside the profile. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093
Vol. 2A Type 3/Table 2-20 and Vol. 2B SUBSS pp. 4-695–4-696; Vol. 1
§§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8. See the [CPU
contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37aq--bounded-masked-range-long64-subss-xmm-register-pairs),
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37aq--bounded-masked-range-long64-subss-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37aq-bounded-masked-range-subss-register-pair).

## S2-37ar — MULPD register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented strict schema-v2 profile `s2-long-mulpd-registers-v1` for
canonical Long64 register-only `66 0F 59 /r`, including all 256 XMM pairs.
Execution is interpreter-only, uses pre-execution snapshots and the existing
raw binary64 multiplication helper, and replaces the whole destination only
after both lanes pass exception processing. MXCSR OM=UM=1 is required; DAZ and
reserved bits are rejected. The independent testkit oracle uses raw integer
significands and no host FP or production helpers. A tininess erratum corrected
runtime and oracle behavior to use the exponent of the precision-rounded result
with unbounded exponent (WPR.exp), not the exact product exponent. For
`0x0010000000000001 × 0x3feffffffffffffe`, RN/RU produce minimum-normal with
PE only independent of FTZ; RD/RZ produce maximum-subnormal with UE|PE, or
positive zero with UE|PE under FTZ. The distinct midpoint product
`minimum-normal × (1−2^-53)` remains tiny after precision rounding and retains
UE|PE in every RC mode. SUBPD already used the production
`tiny_after_precision_rounding` diagnostic and its runner regression remains
unchanged.

The literal fixture verifies exact and inexact lanes, integer-oracle state
validation and backend denial. Focused tests passed for every decoder register
pair and alias, production execution for all 256 pairs, runtime gate/MXCSR and
fetch priority, both minimum-normal product boundaries under all RC settings
with FTZ on and off, signed overflow direction under all RC settings, and
JIT/native rejection. The raw binary32/binary64 multiplication helper test
also verifies WPR tininess for both precisions. The MULPD runner's
`mulpd_literal_pair_rounding_and_backend_denial` covers the new all-RC×FTZ
boundary and the retained midpoint; `mulpd_integer_oracle_handles_tiny_shift128_and_overflow_rounding_boundary`
still passes. The SUBPD, SUBPS, SUBSD and SUBSS runner regressions passed.
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`,
`git diff --check` and `graphify update .` passed. Independent Sol-high review
of the tininess correction found no concrete findings and did not independently
rerun the local commands. Physical
acceptance, memory forms, other modes and full unmasked overflow/underflow
behavior remain open; parent S2-37/S2-38 are not closed. See the [CPU
contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37ar--bounded-masked-range-long64-mulpd-xmm-register-pairs),
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37ar--bounded-masked-range-long64-mulpd-xmm-register-pairs)
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37ar-bounded-masked-range-mulpd-register-pair-profile).

production `tiny_after_precision_rounding` diagnostic. The independent schema
oracle uses raw integer significands and independent rounding logic, with no
host FP or production arithmetic helper.

Implemented strict schema-v2 profile `s2-long-divpd-registers-v1` for canonical
Long64 `66 0F 5E /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, across all 256 XMM pairs. The decoder and

fetches before SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD then TS #NM at CPL0–3 and makes no data
callbacks. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic execution remains closed.

The instruction computes two destination/source binary64 lanes from snapshots.
The implementation classifies NaNs, zero divisors and subnormal operands before
computation, aggregates IE/ZE/DE before arithmetic, and commits pre-event flags
atomically. With pre-events masked it uses the production raw binary64 divide
helper, MXCSR.RC, WPR-based tininess and FTZ. Overflow records OE|PE; tiny
inexact results record UE|PE. An independent raw-u64 rational oracle uses
integer quotient/remainder arithmetic and does not call host FP or production
helpers. The hand-written fixture covers 1/3 and a tiny half-minsub lane.

the successful MXCSR status path; the sticky bit was added and the focused test

raises UE|PE. The oracle tests that tie separately; the neighboring
`minnormal/nextafter(1,+)` vector exercises maxsub versus minnormal rounding.

uses `Binary32::divide_raw_result` with RC/WPR/FTZ for masked execution, and
commits flags before unmasked PE delivery. OM=UM=1 is required; DAZ/reserved
MXCSR bits are rejected. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic execution remains
closed. The independent schema oracle wraps the independent raw-u32 rational
lane helper, not host FP or production arithmetic.

Focused validation passed: `cargo test -p od-testkit divss_ --offline`
(1 oracle test); `cargo test -p od-isa divss_register_decodes --offline`
(1 decoder test); `cargo test -p od-isa divss_runtime_gates --offline`
(1 runtime CPL0–3/fetch/gate test); and the `divss_register_pairs_scalar_events_and_interpreter_only`
runner test (256 pairs, RC/WPR/FTZ, special values, masks, pre/post faults,
malformed/tampered inputs, and backend denial). The focused matrix
also checks masked overflow (OE|PE), unmasked DE suppressing later UE/PE while
preserving XMM/RIP, and the oracle's matching pre-event suppression. The
existing DIVSD pair-alias runtime test passed after restoring its binary64 FTZ
mask; a focused DIVSD FTZ test confirms negative-zero sign and UE|PE behavior.
DIVPD, DIVPS, MUL, and SUB runner regressions and the full od-testkit suite also
passed. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets
--offline`, `python3 tools/check_layout.py`, and `git diff --check` passed.

Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A DIVSS pp. 3-275–3-276 and legacy SSE rows in Table

## S2-37az — ADDPD register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented strict schema-v2 `s2-long-addpd-registers-v1` for canonical
Long64 legacy `66 0F 58 /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, across all 256 XMM register pairs.
The packed binary64 path snapshots both XMM inputs and computes each lane from
the old destination plus source. It gates SSE2 after full instruction fetch,
then checks TS, admits CPL0–3 without data callbacks, and commits the full XMM
destination atomically. Prefix aliases, memory forms, trailing bytes, VEX and
EVEX are rejected. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic execution remains closed.

The runtime uses `Binary64::add_raw_result` for finite lanes and classifies
special operands independently before arithmetic. Packed IE/DE pre-events are
aggregated before post-events; an unmasked pre-event suppresses all new
post-events and the destination write. Tests cover all RC modes, NaN choice
and quieting (including QNaN/SNaN priority), opposite infinities, infinity
plus subnormal DE, NaN suppression of same-lane DE, cross-lane suppression,
PM atomicity, signed zero, exact tiny sums, FTZ, the overflow midpoint versus
larger directed overflow, large exponent gaps, DM masking, old stickies and
OSXMMEXCPT fallback. For finite binary64 sums, an exact subnormal is a multiple
of the minimum subnormal: with FTZ clear it raises neither UE nor PE; FTZ
flushes a nonzero tiny result to signed zero with UE|PE.

Validation passed: `cargo test -p od-isa --offline addpd_` (2 tests), the
focused ADDPD runner matrix (all 256 pairs and aliases plus special values,

overflow/OE correction, removal of the duplicate arm, and independent-oracle
deduplication; no findings remain. Final `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `python3
tools/check_layout.py`, `git diff --check`, and `graphify update .` passed.
Independent Sol-high review is pending.

alignment claim. See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37az--canonical-long64-addpd-xmm-register-pairs),

## S2-37ba — ADDPS register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented strict schema-v2 `s2-long-addps-registers-v1` for canonical
Long64 legacy `0F 58 /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, across all 256 XMM register pairs.
Three-byte low forms and four-byte extended forms use no mandatory prefix and
one canonical REX when needed. The interpreter snapshots both XMM operands and
computes all four old-destination/source binary32 lanes. Full fetch precedes
SSE/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD then CR0.TS #NM; all CPLs work without data callbacks.
SSE is required; SSE2 is not. Memory/prefix aliases and JIT/native/C ABI/
fragment/generic execution are denied.

The production path uses `Binary32::add_raw_result`. It classifies original
inputs first, aggregates IE/DE across all lanes, suppresses post flags and the
whole XMM write on an unmasked pre-event, and commits status before PM delivery.
The profile masks overflow and underflow, while PM remains caller-selectable.
It covers NaN selection/quieting, invalid opposite infinities, infinity plus
subnormal DE, MXCSR rounding/FTZ, directed overflow, exact tiny results,
large-gap DE|PE, old stickies, SSE gate ordering, and destination/source alias.
The four-lane FTZ=1 matrix combines SNaN+1 (IE), minsub+1 (DE|PE),
maxfinite+maxfinite (OE|PE), and `00800001+80800000` (UE|PE): with masks on,
the aggregate status is `0x3b`. Lane permutations prove no early exit; with
IM or DM unmasked, only the newly discovered pre-event bits `0x03` commit and
the whole destination write is suppressed. A masked pre-event plus PM=0
commits all flags before #XM and also leaves XMM/RIP unchanged.
The independent schema oracle performs raw-u32 integer rounding and uses no
host FP or production arithmetic helper.

Validation passed: `cargo test -p od-isa --offline addps_` (4 tests),
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline addpd_` (2 tests), the two ADDPS oracle/schema
tests, and `cargo test -p od-testkit --offline` (441 tests). The literal
fixture's interpreter run passed. ADDPD and ADDPS runtime checks both reject
DAZ, reserved MXCSR bits, OM=0, and UM=0 without changing architectural state.
Previously completed focused regressions passed for ADDPD, SUBPD/SUBPS/SUBSD/
SUBSS, MULPD/MULPS/MULSD/MULSS, and DIVPD/DIVPS/DIVSD/DIVSS. The
CVTSD2SI admission regression also passed after reverting an unrelated test
edit. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets
--offline`, `python3 tools/check_layout.py`, `git diff --check`, and
`graphify update .` passed. Independent Sol-high review found no remaining
issues.

rows in Table 2-27. The p. 3-21 Type 2/Table 2-19 note is for VEX forms, not
legacy ADDPS. No memory alignment or physical-acceptance claim is made. See the

## S2-37bc — ADDSS register-pair interpreter profile (2026-10-30)

Implemented strict schema-v2 `s2-long-addss-registers-v1` for canonical
Long64 legacy `F3 0F 58 /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, across all 256 XMM pairs. Low forms
are four bytes; extended forms use one adjacent REX `41`, `44` or `45` after F3
for five bytes. Memory, 66/F2, reordered/repeated/redundant prefixes, REX.W/X/
40, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are rejected. The profile is interpreter-only;
ADDSS requires SSE, not SSE2. Full fetch precedes SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD then TS #NM
at CPL0–3, with no data callbacks.

Execution snapshots both XMM operands, computes only `old_destination.low32 +
source.low32`, preserves destination.high96, and ignores source.high96. The
production scalar path uses `Binary32::add_raw_result`. It checks original
operands first: first NaN wins, selected SNaN is quieted, any SNaN raises IE,
QNaN alone does not, and NaNs suppress DE. Opposite-sign infinities raise IE
and return `ffc00000`; infinity plus subnormal raises DE. Unmasked IE/DE commits
only pre-event status and suppresses post flags and destination/RIP retirement.
The profile requires MXCSR.OM=1 and UM=1, rejects DAZ/reserved bits, and accepts
RC, FTZ, IM/DM/ZM/PM and prior sticky status. Same-sign zeros retain sign;
exact cancellation is -0 only for round-down. The positive overflow-boundary
midpoint uses OE|PE for RN/RU and PE-only for RD/RZ; maxfinite+maxfinite reports OE|PE in all
rounding modes. The WPR exponent after p=24 rounding determines tininess. Exact
same-format tiny sums with FTZ clear raise no UE/PE; FTZ flushes nonzero tiny
results to signed zero with UE|PE. Unmasked PM commits status but preserves
XMM/RIP/retirement.

The independent testkit oracle is a scalar raw-u32 wrapper over its independent
ADDPS lane implementation, with no host floating-point or production helper.
The handwritten fixture covers `1 + 2^-24`, high96 preservation, and ignored
source-high canaries. Runtime tests cover every pair and aliases, positive and
negative halfway ties, all RC values, directed overflow, exact/FTZ tiny results,
large-gap DE|PE, NaN order/quieting, opposite infinities, infinity plus
subnormal, IE/DE and PM atomicity, invalid MXCSR, full-fetch/gate ordering,
CPL0–3, instruction budget, no callbacks, malformed encodings, fixture
tampering, and JIT/native denial.

Validation passed: four ADDSS-specific od-isa tests; the ADDSS testkit oracle
and schema test; full `cargo test -p od-isa --offline --quiet` (1,574 tests);
full `cargo test -p od-testkit --offline --quiet` (443 tests); and full
`cargo test -p od-runner --offline --test fixture_v2` (433 tests, including
ADDPD/ADDPS and DIV/MUL/SUB regressions). Focused runner execution confirmed
literal scalar output, DE-only atomicity, backend denial, malformed REX
rejection, and snapshot tamper detection. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets
--offline`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `python3 tools/check_layout.py`,
`git diff --check`, and `graphify update .` also passed.
Independent `gpt-6.1-sol` review found no remaining code findings; one old
ADDPS negative vector was removed because its F3 form is now valid ADDSS. No
physical x86 execution was performed, memory operands and other modes remain
outside this profile, and S2-37/S2-38 remain open.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A ADDSS pp. 3-24–3-25 and legacy SSE rows on
p. 2-28; generic SSE/CR0/CR4 gates and SIMD exception handling; Vol. 1
§§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.2–11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; Intel
Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13. The p. 3-25 Type 3/Table 2-20 note
references VEX forms, not legacy ADDSS. The description's apparent copy/paste
errors are not repeated; this profile follows the opcode row and low32
Operation semantics. See the [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37bc--canonical-long64-addss-xmm-register-pairs),
[CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37bc--canonical-long64-addss-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37bc-addss-register-pair-profile).

## S2-37bd — CVTPD2PS register-pair interpreter profile

Added canonical Long64 `66 0F 5A /r` register-form decode and the strict
schema-v2 `s2-long-cvtpd2ps-registers-v1` profile. Runtime uses explicit SSE2,
CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT gates and a raw-bit narrowing helper. It
snapshots both source lanes, writes the two binary32 lanes into destination.low64,
zeros destination.high64 on success, and preserves the entire old destination on
pre-event and post-PM faults. IE/DE pre-events are aggregated before conversion
post-events; FTZ, WPR tininess, sticky flags and numeric exception delivery are
covered by the local oracle. Intel Vol. 1 §§10.2.3.3 and 11.5.2.5 describe FTZ
as the masked-underflow response, which flushes tiny results and sets UE|PE.
The fixture checks an exact minimum subnormal with FTZ set as well as adjacent
subnormal rounding boundaries.

The literal fixture checks 1+2^-24 conversion, lane routing, poison destination,
upper-zeroing, narrow-to-subnormal and overflow edges, FTZ, SNaN status, an
unmasked DE fault, and JIT/native denial. Decoder coverage enumerates 256 XMM
pairs and malformed prefix/form examples. An independent raw-integer
binary64-to-binary32 oracle does not call production conversion code or host
floating point. The focused `od-isa` decode and direct-execution tests passed (all 256 XMM
pairs, including aliases); the focused `od-runner` integration fixture passed.
All 443 `od-testkit` tests passed. Existing CVTPD2DQ, CVTTPD2DQ, DIVPD, MULPD,
ADDPD and SUBPD `od-isa` regression filters passed. Workspace check, layout,
format verification and final graph refresh were run for the completed change.
This remains local interpreter
coverage: no physical CPU, memory form, generic/JIT/native, C ABI or parent
S2-37/S2-38 completion is claimed.


## S2-37be — CVTSD2SS register-pair interpreter profile

Implemented schema-v2 interpreter profile `s2-long-cvtsd2ss-registers-v1` for all 256 canonical Long64 XMM register pairs. Decoder, schema parser and runner accept only legacy `F2 [canonical optional REX 41/44/45] 0F 5A /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, with lengths 4/5. Memory, malformed/redundant/reordered prefixes, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are refused. Full fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM at CPL0–3; no data callbacks occur. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic admission remains closed.

The interpreter snapshots source XMM before writing and narrows only source.low64 under MXCSR.RC through `Binary32::narrow_from_binary64`. It replaces destination.low32 and preserves destination.high96; source.high64 and old destination are ignored by conversion. Aliases use the source snapshot. MXCSR requires OM=UM=1, DAZ=0 and reserved bits clear. SNaN/subnormal inputs raise IE/DE pre-events. Overflow raises OE|PE; tiny inexact results raise UE|PE. FTZ flushes a nonzero tiny result to signed zero with UE|PE, including exact tiny values, per Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13 p.2. An unmasked pre-event commits only IE/DE before fault; an unmasked post-event commits status while preserving the full destination, RIP and retirement. OSXMMEXCPT selects #XM versus SIMD-generated #UD.

The testkit's independent raw-u64 integer oracle validates conversion results and exception state without production conversion helpers or host floating point. Verification passed:

- `cargo test -p od-isa cvtsd2ss_decodes_all_canonical_register_pairs_and_rejects_neighbors --offline` — 256 decoder pairs and malformed encoding neighbors.
- `cargo test -p od-isa cvtsd2ss_fetch_and_sse2_gates_precede_execution_at_every_cpl --offline` — CPL0–3, full-fetch priority, SSE2/EM/OSFXSR before TS, and no data callbacks.
- `cargo test -p od-runner cvtsd2ss_register_pairs_rounding_ftz_exceptions_and_denial --offline` — all register pairs/aliases, RC and FTZ boundaries, NaN payloads, overflow/tiny classes, IE/DE/PE masks and atomic faults, gate priority, malformed schema, and JIT/native denial.

No confirmed unresolved defect was found; no entry was added to `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. Physical x86 acceptance, memory forms and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTSD2SS pp. 3-234–3-235. Type 3/Table 2-20 on p. 3-235 refers to VEX forms, not this legacy encoding. Generic gates and exception delivery also use Intel Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.2–11.5.3; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; and Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13 p.2.

## S2-37bf — CVTPI2PD memory interpreter profile

Implemented `s2-long-cvtpi2pd-memory-rax-v1` as a strict interpreter-only profile for only `66 0F 2A 00`, budget 1 and stop RIP=entry+4. Decoder/schema refuse register source, other ModR/M/address forms, any REX/additional prefix, VEX/EVEX and trailing code bytes. Full fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM. With AC clear and MXCSR within `0x0000ffbf`, execution performs one eight-byte read from canonical48 `[RAX..RAX+7]`, converts both little-endian signed i32 lanes exactly, writes XMM0 only, and preserves MXCSR. It leaves x87 and memory untouched and generates no SIMD FP exception. Read failure rolls back locally; this does not claim guest #PF delivery. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic dispatch remain closed.

The testkit oracle uses independent integer bit construction. The literal fixture has asymmetric i32 extrema at an unaligned RAX. The runner matrix covers ±0/±1, extrema, 2^24 boundaries, NaN-shaped values, RC/sticky MXCSR preservation, SSE2 gate priority, malformed/tampered cases and JIT/native denial. Direct `od-isa` tests cover one read, XMM/MXCSR/x87 canaries, pending x87 state, unaligned address with AC clear, canonical-end overflow, AC=1 refusal, full-fetch gate priority and rollback after a local injected read error.

Focused verification passed: `cargo test -p od-isa cvtpi2pd --offline` (4 tests) and `cargo test -p od-runner cvtpi2pd_memory_profile --offline` (1 schema/oracle/backend test). `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `python3 tools/check_layout.py`, `git diff --check`, and Graphify update also passed. No confirmed unresolved defect was found. This slice does not claim physical x86 acceptance or guest #PF delivery for injected local read failures. Source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTPI2PD p. 3-223 and Vol. 1 SSE2 gate rules.

## S2-37bh — CVTTPS2PI MM0,XMM1 masked register profile

Implemented exact Long64 `0F 2C C1` in the schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-cvttps2pi-register-masked-v1`. It fetches the full three-byte instruction before SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM, allows CPL0–3, performs no data callback and retires exactly once. Memory/alternate registers/prefixes/REX/VEX/EVEX/trailing bytes are refused. MXCSR admission requires supported mask `0x0000ffbf`, IM=PM=1, while x87 requires no pending exception (`FSW & 0x80ff == 0`).

The source snapshot is XMM1.low64 only. Two binary32 lanes truncate toward zero independent of MXCSR.RC through the existing integer-only conversion helper. Masked invalid results are `0x80000000`; exact -2^31 remains valid. IE and PE are aggregated independently, sticky flags are preserved and DE is not raised. Results overwrite physical x87 register 0 as the MM0 view, with exponent bits 79:64 set to `ffff`; TOP becomes zero and all tags become valid. Other x87 payload/state and all XMM state remain unchanged.

The handwritten fixture anchors a fractional lane plus QNaN, high64 poison and nonzero incoming TOP/tag state. The runner tests cover zeros, positive/negative fractions, integer limits, QNaN/SNaN/infinity/subnormals, all RC values, IE+PE aggregation, old sticky flags, TOP variations, gate priority, malformed encodings, result tampering and JIT/native denial. The independent schema oracle uses raw-bit conversion and does not invoke the production `Binary32` helper.

Verification passed: `cargo test -p od-isa cvttps2pi --offline` (3 tests, including CPL0–3 success and truncated-fetch priority over SSE gates), `cargo test -p od-runner cvttps2pi --offline` (1 fixture matrix including fabricated error-code rejection), `cargo test -p od-testkit --offline` (443 tests), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `python3 tools/check_layout.py` (48 required directories, 6 crate scaffolds, 14 instruction scopes), `git diff --check`, and `graphify update .` (10,019 nodes, 21,159 edges, 313 communities). No physical x86 acceptance is claimed. No confirmed new issue was established; the pre-existing ISSUE-028 remains an unverified external CVTPI2PS observation and is not evidence for this register-source profile. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTTPS2PI p. 3-252; Vol. 3B §25.25.3 Table 25-5 p. 25-23; Vol. 3A §15.2 pp. 15-2–15-3 Table 15-2; Vol. 1 SSE, MXCSR and x87/MMX shared-state rules.

The exact Ubuntu 7.0.0-38.38 built-in kernel ELF was scanned across `.text`, `.init.text`, `.altinstr_aux`, `.altinstr_replacement` and `.exit.text`. ## S2-37br — CVTPD2PI MM0,[RAX] aligned m128 memory profile

Implemented the separate schema-v2 interpreter-only Long64 profile for exact
`66 0F 2D 00`, one instruction, budget 1 and stop RIP+4. The decoder fetches
all four bytes before the local SSE2 gates: unavailable CPUID.SSE2 (bit 26),
CR0.EM or CR4.OSFXSR produce #UD, then CR0.TS produces #NM. This priority is a
bounded local policy. CPL0–3 are accepted.

The source is exactly one 16-byte m128 at RAX. The full canonical48 span and
16-byte alignment are checked before the sole read. Misalignment raises
#GP(0) before callback at every CPL independent of RFLAGS.AC; aligned AC=0 and
AC=1 are accepted. MXCSR is limited to `0xffbf` with IM=PM=1, and strict
admission requires `FSW & 0x80ff == 0`; pending-x87 #MF delivery is not modeled.

Each raw binary64 lane is rounded to signed i32 according to MXCSR.RC and only
then range-checked. `0x41dfffffffffffff` is invalid for nearest/upward, but is
valid `i32::MAX` with PE for downward/toward-zero. `0xc1e0000000000001` is
invalid only for downward rounding; the other modes produce valid
`i32::MIN` with PE. NaN, infinity and rounded out-of-range values produce
`0x80000000` and IE. Valid inexact lanes set PE; lane status is OR-combined,
existing status/control bits remain sticky, and DE is not raised. After one
successful read, physical MM0 receives the two i32 values and exponent word
`ffff`, TOP becomes zero and all tags valid, and all other x87 state is

## S2-37cf — CVTSI2SS XMM0,qword ptr [RAX] m64 memory profile

Implemented exact legacy `F3 48 0F 2A 00` under separate strict schema-v2
profile `s2-long-cvtsi2ss-memory64-rax-v1`. It fetches all five bytes, applies
SSE-bit-25/EM/OSFXSR `#UD` then TS `#NM` local gates, and admits CPL0–3. A
missing SSE state after prerequisite gates produces local `Unsupported` rather
than panicking. Checked canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+7]` precedes exactly one 8-byte
little-endian read; unaligned access is allowed with local AC=0. Pre-read
refusals and read errors leave CPU state unchanged.

The raw signed i64 converts directly to binary32 using MXCSR.RC. The oracle
independently parses the fixture's eight source bytes as i64 and uses integer
rounding only; it does not use host FP, a register-source parser, or production
conversion helpers. This direct conversion is important for
`0x0040000040000001`: nearest-even produces `0x5a800001`, while a binary64
intermediate would discard the low +1 and double-round incorrectly. Only
XMM0.low32 changes; high96 and unrelated SSE/GPR/x87 state remain unchanged.
PE is sticky-ORed only for inexact conversions. Exact conversions add no flag,
and no signed-i64 input can cause binary32 overflow.

The profile requires supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0, PM=1, and AC=0;
all RC/FTZ modes, other supported masks, and incoming status bits are admitted.
PM=0/DAZ=1/reserved MXCSR controls are strict-schema malformed cases. AC=1 is
a valid runtime `Unsupported` fixture with no data read or state mutation, checked
through full-state equality. The fixture comparison mask remains `INTEGER_FLAGS`
only and cannot request comparison of AC itself. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic execution
remain closed; portable classifier and runner denial are not physical execution
claims.

negative fixture returning local `Unsupported` before span/read. Read failure

are preserved. The local profile requires SSE2 bit 26, supported MXCSR mask
`0xffbf`, DAZ=0, IM=DM=1; PM may be clear. RC and FTZ are irrelevant.

### S2-37dd — SQRTPS XMM0,m128 [RAX]

Implemented strict schema-v2 interpreter profile `s2-long-sqrtps-memory-rax-v1` for exact Long64 `0F 51 00` (`SQRTPS XMM0,m128 [RAX]`), length three. Full fetch precedes SSE (`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`), CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD and CR0.TS #NM gates; SSE2 is not required. The masked-only profile requires XMM/MXCSR state, supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, clear reserved/DAZ/FTZ bits and all six exception masks. RC modes and previous sticky flags are accepted; unmasked/#XM remains closed.

RAX is required to be 16-byte aligned regardless of AC/CPL. The canonical48 span `[RAX,RAX+15]` is checked before exactly one `read16`; misalignment or invalid span faults before callback, and a read error is atomic. Results use only the four memory-source lanes, so a poisoned prior XMM0 cannot influence output. `Binary32::sqrt_raw_result(RC)` provides lane semantics: negative nonzero including negative subnormal/−∞ contributes IE and `0xffc00000`; SNaN is quieted under the helper policy and contributes IE; QNaN passes; positive subnormal contributes DE; inexact roots contribute PE. IE/DE/PE are aggregated with same-lane ordering and ORed into old stickies. Success replaces all XMM0 and advances RIP by three while preserving GPR, RFLAGS, other XMM, RAM and other state. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment paths remain closed.

The fixture and independent raw-bit integer `independent_sqrtps` oracle cover all four RC modes, signed zeros, infinities, normal/subnormal values, negative normal/subnormal, QNaN/SNaN, sqrt(2), mixed `[-1, min-positive-subnormal, 2, SNaN]` with IE|DE|PE, poisoned XMM0, strict schema/result/backend tampering, gate/fetch priority, zero/one reads, alignment/AC/canonical span, and read-error rollback. The fixture oracle does not call production helpers or host floating point.

### S2-37cy — MAXSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]

Implemented the local interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-maxss-memory-rax-v1` for exact `F3 0F 5F 00`. The instruction fetches four bytes and performs one four-byte read after SSE/EM/OSFXSR/TS gates and canonical48 validation of `[RAX,RAX+3]`. SSE is CPUID.01H:EDX[25], not SSE2. AC=1 is a local Unsupported refusal before span validation/read; AC=0 admits unaligned m32. Local MXCSR requires supported mask `0xffbf`, all six exception masks `0x1f80`, DAZ=FTZ=0, and reserved bits 16–31 clear; any RC and prior IE/DE sticky history are accepted. MAXSS returns raw memory bits on ties (including signed zeros) or any NaN. NaNs raise IE; DE is raised only for subnormal operands when neither input is NaN. Success modifies only XMM0.low32 and effective IE/DE stickies, preserving XMM0.high96 and all other state. Read failures are atomic. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment paths remain closed.

## S2-30da — bounded `FMULP ST(i), ST(0)`

## S2-30cq — bounded `FSUB ST(0), ST(i)`

Added bounded FCW precision execution for exact bare Long64 `D8 E0..E7`.
Admission mirrors S2-30cp: present x87 state, no FCS/FDS selectors, one of the
twelve all-masked PC24/53/64 FCWs, clean required FSW fields, Valid tags, and
canonical nonzero Normal operands. The normalized exponent gap is checked at
≤64 before the arithmetic helper. FSUB is computed by flipping the sign bit
on a validated local RHS copy and passing both operands to the existing
S2-29ae addition precision helper. Source payloads and all unselected state
remain unchanged.

Only finite Normal outputs are admitted; cancellation/zero (including `i=0`),
subnormal, overflow, malformed operands and gap>64 reject atomically. Success
commits physical TOP, accumulates PE, replaces C1 from the helper's pre-carry
`incremented` diagnostic, preserves C0/C2/C3 by the established local policy,
records old RIP in FIP, advances by two and retires once. Fetch faults, STOP
and zero budget do not commit; no data access occurs. `DC` reverse, `DE` pop,
JIT/native and physical x86 acceptance remain closed; bounded `D8 E8..EF`
FSUBR is defined by S2-30cr.

## S2-30cv — bounded reverse `FSUB ST(i), ST(0)`

Added direct FCW precision execution for exact bare Long64 `DC E8..EF`. It
rounds `ST(i) - ST(0)` through the existing S2-29ae addition precision helper,
after validating the original Valid-tagged canonical nonzero Normal operands
and the normalized exponent gap≤64. The sign is flipped only in a local copy
of ST(0). Only finite Normal results are admitted, and `i=0` remains an
atomic cancellation refusal. The prior S2-30i exact-result set is covered by
the p64 equal-exponent path; tests compare literal results and diagnostics
against the unchanged exact helper.

On success, only old physical `(TOP+i)&7` changes. PE is sticky, C1 is replaced
from `incremented`, C0/C2/C3 remain preserved by local policy, FIP receives
old RIP, RIP advances by two and the instruction retires once. Source and
unrelated state remain unchanged, and there is no data access. D8/DC neighbors
and DE pop behavior remain unchanged. JIT/native, general x87 exceptions and
physical x86 acceptance remain closed.

across TOP/index, FCW, signs and prior PE/C1 state. Additional literals cover
midpoint/adjacent and negative directed rounding, direct versus double
rounding, gaps 0/1/63/64 and 65+, alias/cancellation and malformed/range
refusals, full-state atomicity, execution boundaries, no data access, the
prior exact-result domain, max carry, minimum Normal, ±2^-63 and upper
exponent boundaries. Unsupported FCW/FSW, selector and tag refusals use
noncancelling baselines. The decoder's existing exhaustive DC ModR/M and prefix
checks remain unchanged.

## S2-30cw — bounded reverse `FSUBR ST(i), ST(0)`

Added direct FCW precision execution for exact bare Long64 `DC E0..E7`. It
computes old `ST(0) - ST(i)` into old physical `(TOP+i)&7`, without a pop, by
reusing `bounded_x87_fsub_st0_sti_result`; no new arithmetic helper or exact
fallback is introduced. Admission requires present x87 state, absent FCS/FDS,
one of twelve all-masked PC24/53/64 FCWs, `FSW & 0x80df == 0`, Valid tags,
canonical nonzero Normal operands and normalized exponent gap≤64. Alias `i=0`
cancels and is atomically Unsupported. Only finite Normal exact or rounded
results are accepted; the previous S2-30l exact domain is preserved by the
p64 equal-exponent path.

Success changes only old physical `ST(i)`, makes PE sticky, replaces C1 from
`incremented`, preserves TOP/tags/source and unrelated x87 state, records FIP,
advances RIP by two, retires once and performs no data access. Existing
exhaustive DC ModR/M/prefix decoder tests remain in force. Native/JIT, general
x87 exception delivery and physical x86 acceptance remain outside this slice.

## S2-37dn — MULSD XMM0,m64 [RAX]

Implemented the exact legacy `F2 0F 59 00` strict interpreter-only profile. It fetches the full encoding before SSE2/#NM gates, admits only masked MXCSR with DAZ/FTZ clear, permits all RC and sticky histories, refuses AC before the span/read, validates canonical endpoints and performs one unaligned-capable read8. Execution multiplies old XMM0.low64 by the actual memory RHS through the raw binary64 kernel, merges IE/DE/OE/UE/PE and preserves upper state. Other backend/profile paths remain closed.

Layout reports the isolated worktree `.git` pointer and two absent historical oracle manifests recorded under ISSUE-023. Independent Sol/high review is clean (od-isa MULSD 5/5; runner matrix 1/1, 6,400 cases); no physical x86 acceptance is claimed. helper for old `ST(i)/ST(0)`, writes old physical `(TOP+i)&7` without popping,

### S2-37do — DIVSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]

Added the strict interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-divss-memory-rax-v1` for exact legacy `F3 0F 5E 00`. It requires Long64/SSE gates and complete fetch before #UD/#NM, admits masked MXCSR (`0xffbf`, all masks set, DAZ/FTZ/reserved clear), and accepts all RC/sticky histories. AC=1 refuses before span/read; AC=0 allows unaligned m32. Checked `RAX+3` and canonical48 endpoints precede one read4 with rollback on failure.

The executor reuses `Binary32::divide_raw_result`, and the independent raw-u32 `independent_divss` oracle receives the memory RHS. It preserves XMM0.high96 and unrelated state, merges IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE, handles original NaN before ZE/DE/output flags, and uses WPR tininess-after-rounding. The 5,120-run matrix crosses 20 operand pairs × four RC × 64 sticky histories, asserting StopAddress/snapshot/retirement before oracle validation. Includes NaN orders, invalid division, ZE/DE distinctions, exact tiny, WPR underflow and overflow. Direct checks cover runtime MXCSR denial, fetch/gates, AC/span/read rollback, tampering and JIT denial. Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A p. 3-276 Type 3 note is VEX-specific and does not apply to legacy DIVSS. No physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

Validation: `od-isa` 1,824; `od-testkit` 455; runner 118 unit + 495 fixture tests, including 5,120 DIVSS matrix executions; workspace all-target offline check, fmt, diff check and Graphify passed. Layout check reports the isolated-worktree `.git` marker and two absent historical `work/stage*-oracle` manifest links. Independent Sol/high review is clean after backend result-guard and citation corrections. See [standalone report](S2_37DO_DIVSS_MEMORY.md). ## S2-37dx — DIVPD XMM0,m128 [RAX]

Added a dedicated strict schema-v2, interpreter-only memory profile for exact
legacy `66 0F 5E 00`; the register-pair DIVPD path remains separate. The profile
requires SSE2, complete fetch before #UD/#NM gates, masked MXCSR with DAZ/FTZ
clear, and aligned canonical `[RAX,RAX+15]` before one read16. Two lanes divide
old XMM0 values by the actual memory RHS through the raw Binary64 core, aggregate
IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE, and commit only after successful memory access.

## S2-38o — exact Long64 MINSD with unmasked memory IM/DM exits

Added a distinct strict schema-v2 interpreter profile for exact `F2 0F 5D 00`
`MINSD XMM0,m64 [RAX]`. It reuses only MINSD's S2-38g immutable control
contract; CR0.MP is fixed to one. The S2-37cw masked memory and S2-38g register
profiles are unchanged. Complete fetch and SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD gates precede TS
#NM, XMM/MXCSR admission, AC refusal, checked canonical span and exactly one
read8. Address and read failures leave state and retirement unchanged.

The operation classifies source bits before selecting raw memory source 2 for
NaNs and ties. When both IM/DM are masked, IE takes priority over DE. If either
mask is open, new IE|DE is committed on one #XM or arithmetic #UD exit and the
complete XMM0 write and retirement are suppressed. Success changes XMM0.low64,
sticky bits and RIP only. Three literal fixtures and the independent raw-u64
schema oracle cover masked mixed QNaN/subnormal source selection, exact memory
SNaN payload preservation, and unmasked QNaN delivery. Five ISA tests cover fetch/gate order, fetch and memory rollback, neighboring
forms, unaligned reads, selector ties, the event matrix and RC×64 sticky
histories across event/mask combinations. The runner fixture test verifies
control echo, tampering, JIT/native denial, and CLI rejection of forged `jit`
and `native_x86` backend labels.

binary 125 and runner `fixture_v2` 522; x86-runner 8 library + 4 binary;

refresh (11,858 nodes, 25,727 edges, 334 communities). Sol/high review is clean
after fixing forged JIT/native result acceptance and adding required
tie/fault/RC coverage. Main layout validation passes. No physical x86

## Main integration: S2-38u

S2-38u is the exact Long64 legacy `0F 2F 00` COMISS XMM0,m32 `[RAX]`
interpreter-only invalid profile. Admission requires the documented SSE,
CR0/CR4, MXCSR and CPL conditions; AC=1 refuses before data access, while
canonical span validation precedes exactly one four-byte read. A subnormal in
either operand after a successful read yields Unsupported without state
commit. QNaN and SNaN set IE; masked completion updates comparison flags, and
unmasked IE suppresses RFLAGS/RIP/retirement while reporting `#XM` or
arithmetic `#UD` per OSXMMEXCPT. Native/JIT remain closed.

OSXMMEXCPT × old sticky-status cases, finite/infinity/zero relations, five
literal fixtures, gate/fetch ordering, AC/span priority, schema and result
tampering, and forged backend labels. ISA unit tests cover CPL variation and
read-error rollback. On main, checks passed: od-isa

all-target offline check, and formatting. Sol/high review is clean. Graphify
reports 12,054 nodes, 26,189 edges and 366 communities; labels were not
refreshed without an LLM API key. `od-x86-runner` and physical x86 were not
run. ISSUE-033 remains open for the existing mixed NaN/denormal profile audit;
Stage 2 remains open. See [standalone report](S2_38U_COMISS_MEMORY_INVALID_ONLY.md),
[CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-38u--exact-comiss-memory-invalid-only-profile),
